1: //! The Qt renderer: shared decode core (`RenderTree`) + a sent-state cache
2: //! that produces the delta command batch handed to the C++ Qt layer.
3: //!
4: //! The engine emits diffs, and this renderer forwards diffs: it keeps a mirror
5: //! of what the C++ layer already has (`sent`) and, per frame, emits only the
6: //! commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero** commands. The C++
7: //! layer stays dumb (applies the batch, resets to renderer defaults on
8: //! `RESET_NODE`).
9: 
10: use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
11: 
12: use pathland_core::{value_type, Frame};
13: use pathland_render_core::{HostNode, RenderTree};
14: 
15: use crate::ffi::Command;
16: 
17: /// Mirror of the C++ layer's state for one node.
18: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
19: struct SentNode {
20:     text: Option<String>,
21:     props: HashMap<u16, u32>,
22:     strings: HashMap<u16, String>,
23:     date: Option<(i32, u32)>,
24: }
25: 
26: /// Pseudo-parent for tree roots: id `0` maps to the Qt window's contentItem.
27: pub const CONTENT_ITEM: u32 = 0;
28: 
29: /// The retained Qt renderer. Owns the decoded tree (shared core) and the
30: /// sent-state cache used to produce deltas.
31: pub struct QtRenderer {
32:     tree: RenderTree,
33:     sent: HashMap<u32, SentNode>,
34:     sent_children: HashMap<u32, Vec<u32>>,
35: }
36: 
37: impl Default for QtRenderer {
38:     fn default() -> Self {
39:         Self::new()
40:     }
41: }
42: 
43: impl QtRenderer {
44:     pub fn new() -> Self {
45:         Self {
46:             tree: RenderTree::default(),
47:             sent: HashMap::new(),
48:             sent_children: HashMap::new(),
49:         }
50:     }
51: 
52:     /// The decoded tree (shared renderer core).
53:     pub fn tree(&self) -> &RenderTree {
54:         &self.tree
55:     }
56: 
57:     /// Set the effective color scheme (renderer-derived, never carried by the
58:     /// protocol) and re-resolve every design token — re-emitting the changed
59:     /// nodes' concrete values to the C++ layer.
60:     pub fn set_scheme(&mut self, scheme: pathland_core::tokens::Scheme) {
61:         self.tree.set_scheme(scheme);
62:         let cmds = self.diff();
63:         crate::ffi::apply(&cmds);
64:     }
65: 
66:     /// Apply one opcode frame and forward the resulting delta batch to the
67:     /// C++ layer. Unchanged nodes produce no commands.
68:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
69:         self.tree.apply_frame(frame);
70:         let cmds = self.diff();
71:         crate::ffi::apply(&cmds);
72:     }
73: 
74:     /// Clear the whole scene (`META::RESET`): empty the tree and tell the C++
75:     /// layer to drop every widget.
76:     pub fn reset(&mut self) {
77:         self.tree = RenderTree::default();
78:         self.sent.clear();
79:         self.sent_children.clear();
80:         unsafe { crate::ffi::pathland_qt_layer_reset() };
81:     }
82: 
83:     /// Compute the delta batch vs the sent-state cache.
84:     ///
85:     /// Commands with strings point into `self.tree`'s owned strings; the
86:     /// returned batch is only valid while `self` is not mutated — callers must
87:     /// forward it immediately (as [`Self::apply_frame`] does).
88:     pub fn diff(&mut self) -> Vec<Command> {
89:         let mut cmds = Vec::new();
90: 
91:         // 1. Deletions first: nodes gone from the tree.
92:         let live: HashSet<u32> = self.tree.nodes.keys().copied().collect();
93:         let dead: Vec<u32> = self
94:             .sent
95:             .keys()
96:             .copied()
97:             .filter(|id| !live.contains(id))
98:             .collect();
99:         for id in dead {
100:             cmds.push(Command::delete_node(id));
101:             self.sent.remove(&id);
102:             self.sent_children.remove(&id);
103:         }
104: 
105:         // 2. Creates (pre-order, so a parent exists before its children are
106:         //    inserted, and a child before any insert references it).
107:         let order = self.pre_order();
108:         for &id in &order {
109:             if self.sent.contains_key(&id) {
110:                 continue;
111:             }
112:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();
113:             cmds.push(Command::create_node(id, node.component_type));
114:             self.sent.insert(id, SentNode::default());
115:         }
116: 
117:         // 3. Child order (parents before children already exist), THEN props:
118:         //    the C++ layer attaches a widget to its final parent before its
119:         //    WIDTH/HEIGHT/ALIGNMENT arrive, so FILL/stretch resolve against the
120:         //    real parent (a Layout/positioner/window) instead of the create-time
121:         //    contentItem placeholder. The shared core's DELETE_NODE leaves a
122:         //    ghost in the parent's child list, so filter to live nodes.
123:         for &id in &order {
124:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();
125:             let children: Vec<u32> = node
126:                 .children
127:                 .iter()
128:                 .copied()
129:                 .filter(|c| self.tree.nodes.contains_key(c))
130:                 .collect();
131:             let prev = self.sent_children.entry(id).or_default();
132:             cmds.extend(children_diff(id, prev, &children));
133:             *prev = children;
134:         }
135: 
136:         // 4. Roots are children of the pseudo-parent 0 (window contentItem).
137:         let mut roots: Vec<u32> = order
138:             .iter()
139:             .copied()
140:             .filter(|&id| self.tree.node(id).map_or(false, |n| n.parent.is_none()))
141:             .collect();
142:         roots.sort_unstable();
143:         let prev_roots = self.sent_children.entry(CONTENT_ITEM).or_default();
144:         cmds.extend(children_diff(CONTENT_ITEM, prev_roots, &roots));
145:         *prev_roots = roots;
146: 
147:         // 5. Text + property deltas (after the widget is attached to its final
148:         //    parent). On any property change we re-send the node's *complete*
149:         //    property set (preceded by RESET_NODE), so the C++ layer can reset
150:         //    removed properties to its renderer defaults.
151:         for &id in &order {
152:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();
153:             let s = self.sent.get_mut(&id).unwrap();
154: 
155:             if s.text != node.text {
156:                 cmds.push(Command::set_text(id, node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or("")));
157:                 s.text = node.text.clone();
158:             }
159:             if node.date != s.date {
160:                 if let Some((days, millis)) = node.date {
161:                     cmds.push(Command::set_date(id, days, millis));
162:                 }
163:                 s.date = node.date;
164:             }
165:             let strings = string_props(node);
166:             if node.properties != s.props || strings != s.strings {
167:                 cmds.push(Command::reset_node(id));
168:                 // Emit numeric props in a deterministic order with VALUE last:
169:                 // Qt Quick clamps a control's `value` when `from`/`to` aren't
170:                 // configured yet, so min/max must land before the value.
171:                 let mut props: Vec<(u16, u32)> =
172:                     node.properties.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v)).collect();
173:                 // Order: TEXT_STYLE first (a base typography), then the rest
174:                 // (raw font modifiers override it), with VALUE last (Qt Quick
175:                 // clamps a control's value when from/to aren't configured yet).
176:                 use pathland_core::property_id::{TEXT_STYLE, VALUE};
177:                 props.sort_by_key(|(p, _)| (*p == VALUE, *p != TEXT_STYLE, *p));
178:                 for (prop, value) in &props {
179:                     let vt = value_type_for(*prop);
180:                     cmds.push(Command::set_property(id, *prop, vt, *value));
181:                 }
182:                 for (prop, value) in &strings {
183:                     cmds.push(Command::set_string_property(id, *prop, value));
184:                 }
185:                 s.props = node.properties.clone();
186:                 s.strings = strings;
187:             }
188:         }
189: 
190:         cmds
191:     }
192: 
193:     fn pre_order(&self) -> Vec<u32> {
194:         let mut order = Vec::new();
195:         let mut roots: Vec<u32> = self
196:             .tree
197:             .nodes
198:             .keys()
199:             .copied()
200:             .filter(|&id| self.tree.node(id).map_or(false, |n| n.parent.is_none()))
201:             .collect();
202:         roots.sort_unstable();
203:         for r in roots {
204:             self.walk(r, &mut order);
205:         }
206:         order
207:     }
208: 
209:     fn walk(&self, id: u32, out: &mut Vec<u32>) {
210:         // Guard against ghost children (a node deleted from `tree.nodes` but
211:         // still listed in a parent's `children` after DELETE_NODE).
212:         if !self.tree.nodes.contains_key(&id) {
213:             return;
214:         }
215:         out.push(id);
216:         if let Some(node) = self.tree.node(id) {
217:             for c in node.children.clone() {
218:                 self.walk(c, out);
219:             }
220:         }
221:     }
222: }
223: 
224: /// The string-valued properties a node sends to the C++ layer: its decoded
225: /// strings plus `LIST` properties serialized as CSV (today a `FIT_QUERY`
226: /// threshold table, which the Qt layer parses to measure a fit slot).
227: fn string_props(node: &HostNode) -> HashMap<u16, String> {
228:     let mut props = node.strings.clone();
229:     for (prop, values) in &node.lists {
230:         let csv = values
231:             .iter()
232:             .map(|v| v.to_string())
233:             .collect::<Vec<_>>()
234:             .join(",");
235:         props.insert(*prop, csv);
236:     }
237:     props
238: }
239: 
240: /// The opcode wire's value type for a property (same mapping the emit side
241: /// uses; the C++ layer needs it to interpret the raw u32).
242: fn value_type_for(prop: u16) -> u8 {
243:     if is_f32_property(prop) {
244:         value_type::F32
245:     } else {
246:         value_type::U32
247:     }
248: }
249: 
250: fn is_f32_property(prop: u16) -> bool {
251:     matches!(
252:         prop,
253:         pathland_core::property_id::SPACING
254:             | pathland_core::property_id::WIDTH
255:             | pathland_core::property_id::HEIGHT
256:             | pathland_core::property_id::FONT_SIZE
257:             | pathland_core::property_id::OPACITY
258:             | pathland_core::property_id::BORDER_WIDTH
259:             | pathland_core::property_id::BORDER_RADIUS
260:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING
261:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING_TOP
262:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING_RIGHT
263:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING_BOTTOM
264:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING_LEFT
265:             | pathland_core::property_id::VALUE
266:             | pathland_core::property_id::MIN_VALUE
267:             | pathland_core::property_id::MAX_VALUE
268:             | pathland_core::property_id::STEP_VALUE
269:             | pathland_core::property_id::PROGRESS
270:             | pathland_core::property_id::NAV_CHROME
271:             | pathland_core::property_id::TRANSITION
272:             | pathland_core::property_id::OFFSET_X
273:             | pathland_core::property_id::OFFSET_Y
274:             | pathland_core::property_id::POSITION_X
275:             | pathland_core::property_id::POSITION_Y
276:             | pathland_core::property_id::MIN_WIDTH
277:             | pathland_core::property_id::IDEAL_WIDTH
278:             | pathland_core::property_id::MAX_WIDTH
279:             | pathland_core::property_id::MIN_HEIGHT
280:             | pathland_core::property_id::IDEAL_HEIGHT
281:             | pathland_core::property_id::MAX_HEIGHT
282:             | pathland_core::property_id::LAYOUT_PRIORITY
283:             | pathland_core::property_id::ASPECT_RATIO
284:             | pathland_core::property_id::CONTENT_MODE
285:             | pathland_core::property_id::MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR
286:             | pathland_core::property_id::GRID_COLUMNS
287:             | pathland_core::property_id::GRID_ROWS
288:             | pathland_core::property_id::TEXT_ALIGNMENT
289:             | pathland_core::property_id::MEDIA_POSITION
290:             | pathland_core::property_id::MEDIA_VOLUME
291:             | pathland_core::property_id::MEDIA_RATE
292:     )
293: }
294: 
295: /// Minimal child-order delta: for each index where the old and new children
296: /// differ, remove the stale child and insert the new one at that index.
297: fn children_diff(parent: u32, prev: &[u32], next: &[u32]) -> Vec<Command> {
298:     let mut cmds = Vec::new();
299:     let len = prev.len().max(next.len());
300:     for i in 0..len {
301:         let old = prev.get(i).copied();
302:         let new = next.get(i).copied();
303:         if old == new {
304:             continue;
305:         }
306:         if let Some(c) = old {
307:             cmds.push(Command::remove_child(parent, c));
308:         }
309:         if let Some(c) = new {
310:             cmds.push(Command::insert_child(parent, c, i as u32));
311:         }
312:     }
313:     cmds
314: }

316: #[cfg(test)]
317: mod tests {
318:     use super::*;
319:     use pathland_core::{
320:         category, component_type, init_memory, parameter, tree, value_type, Frame, Guest, Host,
321:         MemoryLayout, Opcode,
322:     };
323:     use pathland_engine::Engine;
324:     use pathland_view::{assign_ids, text, vstack, Configurable, Node, Padding, View, ViewExt};
325: 
326:     /// One persistent engine + ring memory, so consecutive emits are **deltas**
327:     /// (like a live app) rather than full snapshots.
328:     struct Harness {
329:         layout: MemoryLayout,
330:         mem: Vec<u8>,
331:         engine: Engine,
332:     }
333: 
334:     impl Harness {
335:         fn new() -> Self {
336:             let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
337:             let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
338:             init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
339:             Self {
340:                 layout,
341:                 mem,
342:                 engine: Engine::new(),
343:             }
344:         }
345: 
346:         /// Emit `root` (delta against the previous emit) and return the frame's
347:         /// slots + arena copied into owned buffers (`frame spans 0..len`).
348:         /// An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes (returns empty buffers).
349:         fn emit(&mut self, root: &Node) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {
350:             let layout = self.layout;
351:             {
352:                 let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
353:                 guest.begin_frame();
354:                 self.engine.emit(root, &mut guest).unwrap();
355:                 guest.end_frame();
356:             }
357:             let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
358:             let frames = host.frames();
359:             assert!(frames.len() <= 1, "at most one frame per emit");
360:             let Some(f) = frames.first() else {
361:                 return (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
362:             };
363:             let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(f.len() * 16);
364:             for op in f.opcodes() {
365:                 slots.extend_from_slice(&op.to_bytes());
366:             }
367:             let arena = f.arena().to_vec();
368:             (slots, arena)
369:         }
370:     }
371: 
372:     fn apply_emit(r: &mut QtRenderer, h: &mut Harness, root: &Node) {
373:         let (slots, arena) = h.emit(root);
374:         let frame = Frame::from_parts(&slots, &arena, 0, slots.len());
375:         r.tree.apply_frame(&frame);
376:     }

378:     #[test]
379:     fn first_frame_creates_tree_and_props() {
380:         let mut view = vstack![text("ab"), text("cd")]
381:             .with(|v| {
382:                 v.spacing(4.0);
383:             })
384:             .modifiers(Padding(8.0))
385:             .build();
386:         assign_ids(&mut view, &mut 1);
387: 
388:         let mut h = Harness::new();
389:         let mut r = QtRenderer::new();
390:         apply_emit(&mut r, &mut h, &view);
391:         let cmds = r.diff();
392: 
393:         let kinds: Vec<u8> = cmds.iter().map(|c| c.kind).collect();
394:         // Creates for 1,2,3 then per-node reset+props/text, then children.
395:         assert!(kinds.contains(&Command::CREATE_NODE));
396:         assert!(kinds.contains(&Command::RESET_NODE));
397:         assert!(kinds.contains(&Command::SET_TEXT));
398:         assert!(kinds.contains(&Command::SET_PROPERTY));
399: 
400:         // Root (1) is created, reset, gets SPACING + PADDING props.
401:         let root_props: Vec<&Command> = cmds
402:             .iter()
403:             .filter(|c| c.kind == Command::SET_PROPERTY && c.a == 1)
404:             .collect();
405:         assert!(!root_props.is_empty());
406:         let spacing = root_props
407:             .iter()
408:             .any(|c| (c.b & 0xFFFF) as u16 == pathland_core::property_id::SPACING);
409:         assert!(spacing, "root carries SPACING");
410:     }

1: # pathland-render-qt — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** October 20, 2026
4: 
5: The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
6: scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
7: Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
8: 
9: **Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
10: - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
11:   **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
12:   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
13:   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
14: - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
15:   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
16:   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
17:   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative qtmultimedia`).
18: 
19: ## Implemented
20: 
21: - **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
22:   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
23:   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
24:   `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
25:   core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
26: - **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
27:   `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
28:   set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
29:   `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
30: - **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
31:   emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
32:   commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
33:   preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
34:   renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
35:   clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
36:   are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
37:   `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
38: - **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
39:   `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
40:   `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
41:   padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
42:   `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView` (content attaches to its
43:   `contentItem`; fills its parent by default), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
44:   unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
45:   `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
46:   → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
47:   handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
48:   activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
49:   (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
50:   `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
51:   (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
52:   `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
53:   native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
54:   (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
55:   FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
56:   `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family via the `font` `QFont`
57:   property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible, z,
58:   value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
59:   `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
60:   prompt/label→placeholder, image source. **Stack alignment**: a stack's
61:   `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
62:   (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).
63:   **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
64:   `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
65:   slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
66: - **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
67:   *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
68:   attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
69:   the create-time contentItem placeholder.
70: - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
71:   (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
72:   `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
73:   ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
74:   `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
75: - **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
76:   is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
77:   its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
78:   Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
79:   spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
80:   `DELETE`.
81: - **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
82:   `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
83:   renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
84: - **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
85:   fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
86:   shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
87:   concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
88:   init.
89: - **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
90:   `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
91:   C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
92: - **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
93:   an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
94:   idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
95: - **Asset root** (`pathland_qt_set_asset_root` /
96:   `pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root`): web-style `/_pathland/...` image/media
97:   sources resolve against a host-extracted local directory (the Qt analogue of
98:   `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); the Java Qt host extracts `DemoAssets` and
99:   sets it before `runRing`.
100: - **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
101:   on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
102:   `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
103:   `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
104:   a bare program name to Qt.
105: - **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
106:   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
107:   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
108:   shared ring).
109: 
110: - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
111:   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
112:   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
113:   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
114:   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
115:   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
116:   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
117:   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
118:   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
119:   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
120:   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
121:   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
122:   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
123:   **Page sizing:** each page wrapper is anchored to fill the nav container
124:   (`placeDestination`), so the header/content/destination chain is sized and the
125:   destination subtree fills the content area (previously the page wrapper was
126:   attached unsized, collapsing the content to 0×0 and showing only an
127:   overflowing title).
128: 
129: - **Post-merge protocol parity (October 2026)**: the crate was merged onto the
130:   shared `PARAMETER` rename and now maps the protocol surface added on `main`:
131:   - `ICON` (0x0B) → a `Text` item whose glyph is resolved from `ICON_NAME` by a
132:     renderer-owned canonical-name map (unknown names fall back to a dot), with
133:     `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE` reuse (spec/ICONS.md).
134:   - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) → **non-visual** (layout-transparent: created but
135:     never attached) hosting a QML `MediaPlayer` + `AudioOutput`
136:     (spec/MEDIA.md).
137:   - `VIDEO` (0x0A) → a `VideoOutput` surface; `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` binds its
138:     `source` to the referenced controller's `MediaPlayer` (a reference, not a
139:     parent/child edge).
140:   - `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) → a transparent vertical container.
141:   - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` (0x17) → a greedy two-axis slot; its one selected child
142:     fills it.
143:   - `GRID_ROW` (0x1D) → a row-grouping container whose cells flatten into
144:     the parent Grid.
145: - **Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core`): `LIST`-typed properties
146:   (`FIT_QUERY`) decode into `HostNode::lists`, and `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` into
147:   `HostNode::date` — so the Qt layer can measure fit slots and format dates.
148: - **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit measurement**: the slot's `FIT_QUERY` thresholds reach
149:   the C++ layer as CSV; a width change derives the fit index (largest
150:   `minWidth` ≤ allocated width) and reports `FIT_CHANGED` (only when it
151:   changes).
152: - **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: a row's cells attach directly to the parent Grid
153:   (row-major), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.
154: - **`DATE_PICKER`**: `SET_DATE` (days since epoch + millis of day) renders as an
155:   ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field — a QML approximation
156:   (Qt Quick has no native date picker).
157: - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md): pointer `hover`/`leave` (`POINTER_MOVE`
158:   hovering/leaving) from the listener `MouseArea`; `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the
159:   focused text input (component-type/key-listener gated); `FOCUS_CHANGED` /
160:   `EDITING_CHANGED` / `SUBMIT` for text inputs (gated by the matching
161:   `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits); BackSpace is native back unless a text input is
162:   focused (focus-aware, no longer deferred).
163: - **Visual styling layer** (parity with the web/GTK demos):
164:   - `BACKGROUND_COLOR` / `BORDER_*` / `BORDER_RADIUS` render on a background
165:     `Rectangle` behind a container's content (stacks reuse an injected
166:     `pl<id>bg`; plain containers create one lazily); `Rectangle`-backed nodes
167:     set them directly. `RESET_NODE` clears them.
168:   - **Composite control mode** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §2): a `Button` that gains
169:     children is promoted from the native widget to a bare `Item`+`ColumnLayout`
170:     shell that renders the app's `ButtonStyle` body, so `PlainButtonStyle` /
171:     `BorderedButtonStyle` buttons look like the web/GTK ones. Leaf buttons stay
172:     native.
173:   - **Foreground inheritance** (CSS `color`): a container's `COLOR` is inherited
174:     by descendant `Text`/`Icon` that don't set their own.
175:   - **Layout defaults**: cross-axis stretch (`align-items:stretch`) when no
176:     `ALIGNMENT` is set; `Spacer` expands on the main axis; `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
177:   - **`TEXT_STYLE`** applies a base typography (size + weight) that raw
178:     `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT` override; **`SHADOW_*`** draws a best-effort
179:     offset shadow layer.
180: - **Media transport** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`
181:   (play/pause), `MEDIA_POSITION` (seek, seconds→ms), `MEDIA_VOLUME` /
182:   `MEDIA_MUTED` (via `AudioOutput`), `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
183:   `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
184:   `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` reports (reported by the
185:   controller's component type, not gated by `BINDING_ID`; programmatic sets are
186:   echo-suppressed). A play/pause declared before the source is re-applied when
187:   the source lands.
188: - **Layout/property parity**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_*`,
189:   `CONTENT_MODE` (image fit/fill), `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_COLOR` /
190:   `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_RADIUS`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`,
191:   `TRUNCATION_MODE`, and `GRID_COLUMNS` (via the `Layout` attached properties
192:   where applicable).
193: - **Headless test hang fixed**: Qt adds the executable's directory to QML's
194:   implicit import path; a `cargo test` binary lives in a huge `target/debug/deps`
195:   and plugin resolution scanned it for minutes. The shell now drops the
196:   application directory from the engine's import path at init, so
197:   `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` completes in ~2s (no copy-to-temp workaround).
198: 
199: ## Not implemented / gaps
200: 
201: - **`MENU` popup item list**: Qt 6 has no `MenuButton`; the trigger is a
202:   `Button` and the action-item popup is not built (documented gap).
203: - **`COLOR_PICKER`** remains a `Button` approximation (a QML color-swatch popup
204:   is a follow-up); `DATE_PICKER` is an ISO-text QML approximation, not a native
205:   dialog.
206: - **`PICKER` option styling** and `SHAPE` path approximation. Native **leaf**
207:   controls keep Qt Quick Controls' own chrome (background/border); the styling
208:   layer covers containers, composite controls, and `Rectangle`-backed nodes.
209: - **Icons** are renderer-owned glyphs (the canonical `ICON_NAME` → a Unicode
210:   symbol), not the web's SVG/Lucide set — recognizable but not pixel-identical.
211: - **Shadows** are an offset rectangle approximation, not a blurred
212:   `MultiEffect` shadow.
213: - **Keys/events beyond the focused text input**: keys are reported for a focused
214:   text input; keys on other focused controls, `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, and

# pathland-render-qt — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 20, 2026

The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.

**Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
- **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
  **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
  the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
  and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
- **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
  QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
  delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
  needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative qtmultimedia`).

## Implemented

- **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
  Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
  links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
  `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
  core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
- **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
  `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
  set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
  `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
- **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
  emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
  commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
  preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
  renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
  clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
  are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
  `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
- **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
  `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
  `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
  padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
  `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView` (content attaches to its
  `contentItem`; fills its parent by default), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
  unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
  `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
  → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
  handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
  activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
  (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
  `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
  (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
  `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
  native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
  (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
  FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
  `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family via the `font` `QFont`
  property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible, z,
  value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
  `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
  prompt/label→placeholder, image source. **Stack alignment**: a stack's
  `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
  (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).
  **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
  `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
  slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
- **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
  *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
  attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
  the create-time contentItem placeholder.
- **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
  (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
  `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
  ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
  `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
- **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
  is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
  its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
  Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
  spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
  `DELETE`.
- **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
  `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
  renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
- **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
  fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
  shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
  concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
  init.
- **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
  `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
  C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
- **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
  an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
  idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
- **Asset root** (`pathland_qt_set_asset_root` /
  `pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root`): web-style `/_pathland/...` image/media
  sources resolve against a host-extracted local directory (the Qt analogue of
  `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); the Java Qt host extracts `DemoAssets` and
  sets it before `runRing`.
- **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
  on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
  `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
  `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
  a bare program name to Qt.
- **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
  Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
  the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
  shared ring).

- **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
  `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
  page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
  `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
  depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
  chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
  `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
  pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
  is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
  has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
  QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
  container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
  visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
  **Page sizing:** each page wrapper is anchored to fill the nav container
  (`placeDestination`), so the header/content/destination chain is sized and the
  destination subtree fills the content area (previously the page wrapper was
  attached unsized, collapsing the content to 0×0 and showing only an
  overflowing title).

- **Post-merge protocol parity (October 2026)**: the crate was merged onto the
  shared `PARAMETER` rename and now maps the protocol surface added on `main`:
  - `ICON` (0x0B) → a `Text` item whose glyph is resolved from `ICON_NAME` by a
    renderer-owned canonical-name map (unknown names fall back to a dot), with
    `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE` reuse (spec/ICONS.md).
  - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) → **non-visual** (layout-transparent: created but
    never attached) hosting a QML `MediaPlayer` + `AudioOutput`
    (spec/MEDIA.md).
  - `VIDEO` (0x0A) → a `VideoOutput` surface; `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` binds its
    `source` to the referenced controller's `MediaPlayer` (a reference, not a
    parent/child edge).
  - `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) → a transparent vertical container.
  - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` (0x17) → a greedy two-axis slot; its one selected child
    fills it.
  - `GRID_ROW` (0x1D) → a row-grouping container whose cells flatten into
    the parent Grid.
- **Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core`): `LIST`-typed properties
  (`FIT_QUERY`) decode into `HostNode::lists`, and `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` into
  `HostNode::date` — so the Qt layer can measure fit slots and format dates.
- **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit measurement**: the slot's `FIT_QUERY` thresholds reach
  the C++ layer as CSV; a width change derives the fit index (largest
  `minWidth` ≤ allocated width) and reports `FIT_CHANGED` (only when it
  changes).
- **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: a row's cells attach directly to the parent Grid
  (row-major), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.
- **`DATE_PICKER`**: `SET_DATE` (days since epoch + millis of day) renders as an
  ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field — a QML approximation
  (Qt Quick has no native date picker).
- **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md): pointer `hover`/`leave` (`POINTER_MOVE`
  hovering/leaving) from the listener `MouseArea`; `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the
  focused text input (component-type/key-listener gated); `FOCUS_CHANGED` /
  `EDITING_CHANGED` / `SUBMIT` for text inputs (gated by the matching
  `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits); BackSpace is native back unless a text input is
  focused (focus-aware, no longer deferred).
- **Visual styling layer** (parity with the web/GTK demos):
  - `BACKGROUND_COLOR` / `BORDER_*` / `BORDER_RADIUS` render on a background
    `Rectangle` behind a container's content (stacks reuse an injected
    `pl<id>bg`; plain containers create one lazily); `Rectangle`-backed nodes
    set them directly. `RESET_NODE` clears them.
  - **Composite control mode** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §2): a `Button` that gains
    children is promoted from the native widget to a bare `Item`+`ColumnLayout`
    shell that renders the app's `ButtonStyle` body, so `PlainButtonStyle` /
    `BorderedButtonStyle` buttons look like the web/GTK ones. Leaf buttons stay
    native.
  - **Foreground inheritance** (CSS `color`): a container's `COLOR` is inherited
    by descendant `Text`/`Icon` that don't set their own.
  - **Layout defaults**: cross-axis stretch (`align-items:stretch`) when no
    `ALIGNMENT` is set; `Spacer` expands on the main axis; `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
  - **`TEXT_STYLE`** applies a base typography (size + weight) that raw
    `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT` override; **`SHADOW_*`** draws a best-effort
    offset shadow layer.
- **Media transport** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`
  (play/pause), `MEDIA_POSITION` (seek, seconds→ms), `MEDIA_VOLUME` /
  `MEDIA_MUTED` (via `AudioOutput`), `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
  `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
  `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` reports (reported by the
  controller's component type, not gated by `BINDING_ID`; programmatic sets are
  echo-suppressed). A play/pause declared before the source is re-applied when
  the source lands.
- **Layout/property parity**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_*`,
  `CONTENT_MODE` (image fit/fill), `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_COLOR` /
  `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_RADIUS`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`,
  `TRUNCATION_MODE`, and `GRID_COLUMNS` (via the `Layout` attached properties
  where applicable).
- **Headless test hang fixed**: Qt adds the executable's directory to QML's
  implicit import path; a `cargo test` binary lives in a huge `target/debug/deps`
  and plugin resolution scanned it for minutes. The shell now drops the
  application directory from the engine's import path at init, so
  `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` completes in ~2s (no copy-to-temp workaround).

## Not implemented / gaps

- **`MENU` popup item list**: Qt 6 has no `MenuButton`; the trigger is a
  `Button` and the action-item popup is not built (documented gap).
- **`COLOR_PICKER`** remains a `Button` approximation (a QML color-swatch popup
  is a follow-up); `DATE_PICKER` is an ISO-text QML approximation, not a native
  dialog.
- **`PICKER` option styling** and `SHAPE` path approximation. Native **leaf**
  controls keep Qt Quick Controls' own chrome (background/border); the styling
  layer covers containers, composite controls, and `Rectangle`-backed nodes.
- **Icons** are renderer-owned glyphs (the canonical `ICON_NAME` → a Unicode
  symbol), not the web's SVG/Lucide set — recognizable but not pixel-identical.
- **Shadows** are an offset rectangle approximation, not a blurred
  `MultiEffect` shadow.
- **Keys/events beyond the focused text input**: keys are reported for a focused
  text input; keys on other focused controls, `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, and
  `DATE_CHANGED` are not yet reported. Hover/leave use `POINTER_MOVE` (the
  listener mask bit).
- **FILL inside plain positioners**: `GRID` (a `QQuickGrid`) rejects
  `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid
  defers and is skipped (the positioner sizes it). Stacks use `RowLayout`/
  `ColumnLayout` so FILL children stretch properly.
- The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
  does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
  tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
- The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` (the spec table is aspirational) —
  the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
  vehicle.
- `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
  intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
- **Java JNA demo** (`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`) runs the shared
  `SplitNavDemo` (incl. native navigation) via `pathland_qt_run_ring`.
- Lazy views render eagerly.

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (needs Qt6 dev libs; offscreen for the FFI
tests) — the delta diff suite, the end-to-end FFI batch
(`command_batch_crosses_into_cpp_offscreen`), the **full pipeline**
(`renderer_drives_live_qml_scene`: DSL → engine → frame → shared decode →
delta diff → FFI → live QML `Column`/`Text`/`Button`/`Slider` with spacing/value
applied and a delta re-applied), **FILL/Layout stretch**
(`fill_child_stretches_inside_stack`: FILL → `Layout.fillWidth`, fixed →
`Layout.preferredWidth`, stack `ALIGNMENT=FILL` stretches the cross axis, root
anchored to the window), pointer-listener MouseArea attachment
(`pointer_listeners_attach_mousearea`), the event path
(`decode_maps_pointer_and_global_events`, `ring_event_writes_pointer_into_ring_and_wakes`,
`scheme_event_reapplies_without_waking`, `text_event_string_is_length_prefixed`,

284:     /// One persistent engine + ring memory, so consecutive emits are deltas.
285:     struct Harness {
286:         layout: MemoryLayout,
287:         mem: Vec<u8>,
288:         engine: Engine,
289:     }
290: 
291:     impl Harness {
292:         fn new() -> Self {
293:             let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
294:             let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
295:             init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
296:             Self {
297:                 layout,
298:                 mem,
299:                 engine: Engine::new(),
300:             }
301:         }
302: 
303:         fn emit(&mut self, root: &Node) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {
304:             let layout = self.layout;
305:             {
306:                 let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
307:                 guest.begin_frame();
308:                 self.engine.emit(root, &mut guest).unwrap();
309:                 guest.end_frame();
310:             }
311:             let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
312:             let frames = host.frames();
313:             let Some(f) = frames.first() else {
314:                 return (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
315:             };
316:             let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(f.len() * 16);
317:             for op in f.opcodes() {
318:                 slots.extend_from_slice(&op.to_bytes());
319:             }
320:             let arena = f.arena().to_vec();
321:             (slots, arena)
322:         }
323:     }

325:     fn read_text(id: u32) -> String {
326:         let mut buf = [0i8; 256];
327:         let n = unsafe { pathland_qt_layer_widget_text(id, buf.as_mut_ptr(), buf.len() as u32) };
328:         if n == 0 {
329:             return String::new();
330:         }
331:         unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(buf.as_ptr()) }
332:             .to_string_lossy()
333:             .into_owned()
334:     }

456:     /// FILL sizing inside a stack (the "sliver" fix): a WIDTH FILL child
457:     /// stretches via the Layout attached property; a fixed width becomes the
458:     /// Layout preferredWidth; a stack's ALIGNMENT=FILL stretches children on the
459:     /// cross axis.

461:     fn fill_child_stretches_inside_stack() {
462:         with_qt(|| unsafe {
463:             let cmds = [
464:                 Command::create_node(1, component_type::HSTACK),
465:                 Command::create_node(2, component_type::TEXT),
466:                 Command::create_node(3, component_type::TEXT),
467:                 Command::insert_child(1, 2, u32::MAX),
468:                 Command::insert_child(1, 3, u32::MAX),
469:                 Command::insert_child(0, 1, u32::MAX),
470:                 Command::set_property(1, property_id::ALIGNMENT, value_type::F32, 3.0f32.to_bits()),
471:                 Command::set_property(2, property_id::WIDTH, value_type::F32, 100.0f32.to_bits()),
472:                 Command::set_property(3, property_id::WIDTH, value_type::F32, (-1.0f32).to_bits()),
473:                 Command::set_text(2, "a"),
474:                 Command::set_text(3, "b"),
475:             ];
476:             pathland_qt_layer_apply(cmds.as_ptr(), cmds.len() as u32);
477: 
478:             assert_eq!(
479:                 pathland_qt_layer_root_child_count(),
480:                 1,
481:                 "root fills the window"
482:             );
483:             assert_eq!(
484:                 pathland_qt_layer_widget_child_count(1),
485:                 2,
486:                 "both children in the stack"
487:             );
488:             // The root HSTACK wrapper is anchored to the window content (the
489:             // "sliver" fix) instead of hugging its content.
490:             assert_eq!(
491:                 pathland_qt_layer_anchors_fill(1),
492:                 1,
493:                 "root anchored to the window"
494:             );
495:             // Child 2 (fixed width 100) -> Layout.preferredWidth 100.
496:             assert_eq!(pathland_qt_layer_widget_preferred(2, 0), 100.0);
497:             // Child 3 (WIDTH FILL) -> Layout.fillWidth set.
498:             assert_eq!(pathland_qt_layer_widget_fill(3, 0), 1);
499:             // Root ALIGNMENT=FILL -> children fill the cross axis (height).
500:             assert_eq!(pathland_qt_layer_widget_fill(2, 1), 1);
501:             assert_eq!(pathland_qt_layer_widget_fill(3, 1), 1);
502:         });
503:     }

1: // The C++ Qt Quick shell + widget mapping for `pathland-render-qt`.
2: //
3: // Owns the Qt application objects (QGuiApplication / QQuickWindow / QQmlEngine /
4: // a root Item / the QML-facing Bridge) and applies the Rust delta command batch
5: // to QML items: create/delete/insert/remove widgets, set text + properties, and
6: // report control inputs back through the Bridge. The shell is split so tests
7: // can `init` the scene headless (offscreen) and drive `apply` without entering
8: // the event loop.
9: //
10: // Contract: the renderer never drains events — Rust encodes what the Bridge
11: // reports and wakes the host. Programmatic value sets suppress echoes, and only
12: // BINDING_ID/ACTION_ID-gated nodes report interactions (spec/EVENTS.md).

176: // Pathland TEXT_ALIGNMENT enum -> Qt::Alignment (Leading=0, Center=1,
177: // Trailing=2, Fill/Justify=3).
178: int alignmentFor(float code) {
179:     switch (static_cast<int>(code + 0.5f)) {
180:     case 1:
181:         return int(Qt::AlignHCenter);
182:     case 2:
183:         return int(Qt::AlignRight);
184:     case 3:
185:         return int(Qt::AlignJustify);
186:     default:
187:         return int(Qt::AlignLeft);
188:     }

191: // Canonical icon name -> glyph (spec/ICONS.md). The vocabulary is the protocol
192: // contract; the concrete glyph is renderer-owned. Unknown names fall back to a
193: // neutral dot so the node still renders.
194: // Resolve an asset source: `/_pathland/<rest>` -> `<root>/<rest>` when an
195: // asset root is configured, else the source unchanged. Non-`/_pathland/`
196: // sources (absolute paths, file:// URLs) pass through.
197: QUrl resolveAsset(const QString &source, const QString &root) {
198:     const QString prefix = QStringLiteral("/_pathland/");
199:     if (root.isEmpty() || !source.startsWith(prefix)) {
200:         return QUrl(source);
201:     }
202:     QString r = root;
203:     while (r.endsWith('/')) {
204:         r.chop(1);
205:     }
206:     if (r.isEmpty()) {
207:         return QUrl(source);
208:     }
209:     return QUrl::fromLocalFile(r + QStringLiteral("/") + source.mid(prefix.size()));
210: }

353: QQuickItem *createComponent(QQmlEngine *engine, QQuickItem *parent, const char *qml) {
354:     QQmlComponent comp(engine);
355:     comp.setData(QByteArray(qml), QUrl());
356:     if (comp.isError()) {
357:         qWarning() << "component error:" << comp.errorString();
358:         return nullptr;
359:     }
360:     QObject *obj = comp.create();
361:     if (!obj) {
362:         qWarning() << "create failed:" << comp.errorString();
363:         return nullptr;
364:     }
365:     QQuickItem *item = qobject_cast<QQuickItem *>(obj);
366:     if (item && parent) {
367:         item->setParentItem(parent);
368:     }
369:     return item;
370: }

372: // Build the QML snippet for a component type (node id embedded for controls so
373: // their signal handlers can report it).
374: QString qmlFor(uint16_t component, uint32_t id) {
375:     switch (component) {
376:     case PL_COMP_PROXY_VIEW:
377:     case PL_COMP_VSTACK:
378:     case PL_COMP_LAZY_VSTACK:
379:         // A stack renders as a wrapper Item holding an inner ColumnLayout (the
380:         // node's widget is the wrapper; children attach to the layout, whose
381:         // `Layout` attached properties give FILL children a real stretch —
382:         // plain Row/Column reject anchors on their children). Padding is
383:         // carried by `plPad` (drives the layout's anchors.margins + the
384:         // wrapper's implicit size so the wrapper hugs its content).
385:         return QStringLiteral(
386:                    "import QtQuick 2.15\nimport QtQuick.Layouts 1.15\n"
387:                    "Item {\n"
388:                    "  objectName: \"pl%1\"\n"
389:                    "  property real plPad: 0\n"
390:                    "  implicitWidth: lay ? lay.implicitWidth + 2 * plPad : 0\n"
391:                    "  implicitHeight: lay ? lay.implicitHeight + 2 * plPad : 0\n"
392:                    "  Rectangle {\n"
393:                    "    objectName: \"pl%1bg\"\n"
394:                    "    anchors.fill: parent\n"
395:                    "    color: \"transparent\"\n"
396:                    "    z: -1\n"
397:                    "  }\n"
398:                    "  ColumnLayout {\n"
399:                    "    id: lay\n"
400:                    "    objectName: \"pl%1lay\"\n"
401:                    "    anchors.fill: parent\n"
402:                    "    anchors.margins: plPad\n"
403:                    "    spacing: 0\n"
404:                    "  }\n"
405:                    "}")
406:             .arg(id);
407:     case PL_COMP_HSTACK:
408:     case PL_COMP_LAZY_HSTACK:
409:         return QStringLiteral(
410:                    "import QtQuick 2.15\nimport QtQuick.Layouts 1.15\n"
411:                    "Item {\n"
412:                    "  objectName: \"pl%1\"\n"
413:                    "  property real plPad: 0\n"
414:                    "  implicitWidth: lay ? lay.implicitWidth + 2 * plPad : 0\n"
415:                    "  implicitHeight: lay ? lay.implicitHeight + 2 * plPad : 0\n"
416:                    "  Rectangle {\n"
417:                    "    objectName: \"pl%1bg\"\n"
418:                    "    anchors.fill: parent\n"
419:                    "    color: \"transparent\"\n"
420:                    "    z: -1\n"
421:                    "  }\n"
422:                    "  RowLayout {\n"
423:                    "    id: lay\n"
424:                    "    objectName: \"pl%1lay\"\n"
425:                    "    anchors.fill: parent\n"
426:                    "    anchors.margins: plPad\n"
427:                    "    spacing: 0\n"
428:                    "  }\n"
429:                    "}")
430:             .arg(id);
431:     case PL_COMP_ZSTACK:
432:         return QStringLiteral("import QtQuick 2.15\nItem { objectName: \"pl%1\" }").arg(id);
433:     case PL_COMP_GRID:
434:     case PL_COMP_LAZY_VGRID:
435:     case PL_COMP_LAZY_HGRID:
436:         return QStringLiteral("import QtQuick 2.15\nGrid { objectName: \"pl%1\" }").arg(id);
437:     case PL_COMP_SCROLL:
438:         return QStringLiteral(
439:                    "import QtQuick 2.15\nimport QtQuick.Controls 2.15\n"
440:                    "ScrollView { objectName: \"pl%1\"; clip: true }")
441:             .arg(id);
442:     case PL_COMP_TEXT:
443:         // Word-wrap within the allocated width (HTML/SwiftUI behavior); with no
444:         // constraint the implicit width is the unwrapped line, so this is inert.
445:         return QStringLiteral(
446:                    "import QtQuick 2.15\nText { objectName: \"pl%1\"; "
447:                    "wrapMode: Text.WordWrap }")
448:             .arg(id);
449:     case PL_COMP_SPACER:
450:         return QStringLiteral("import QtQuick 2.15\nItem { objectName: \"pl%1\" }").arg(id);
451:     case PL_COMP_DIVIDER:
452:         return QStringLiteral(
453:                    "import QtQuick 2.15\nRectangle { objectName: \"pl%1\"; width: 1; height: 1; "
454:                    "color: \"#E5E7EB\" }")
455:             .arg(id);
456:     case PL_COMP_COLOR:
457:     case PL_COMP_SHAPE:
458:         return QStringLiteral("import QtQuick 2.15\nRectangle { objectName: \"pl%1\" }").arg(id);
459:     case PL_COMP_IMAGE:
460:         return QStringLiteral(
461:                    "import QtQuick 2.15\nImage { objectName: \"pl%1\"; "
462:                    "fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectFit }")
463:             .arg(id);
464:     case PL_COMP_ICON:
465:         // A semantic icon: a Text item whose glyph is resolved from ICON_NAME
466:         // by the renderer (spec/ICONS.md — the glyph mapping is renderer-owned).
467:         return QStringLiteral("import QtQuick 2.15\nText { objectName: \"pl%1\" }").arg(id);
468:     case PL_COMP_SIZE_THAT_FITS:

755: // The fit index for an allocated width: the largest candidate whose minWidth is
756: // <= width (thresholds ascending), clamped to the table (spec/PRIMITIVES.md).
757: int deriveFitIndex(const std::vector<double> &thresholds, double width) {
758:     if (thresholds.empty()) {
759:         return 0;
760:     }
761:     int index = 0;
762:     for (size_t i = 0; i < thresholds.size(); ++i) {
763:         if (thresholds[i] <= width) {
764:             index = static_cast<int>(i);
765:         } else {
766:             break;
767:         }
768:     }
769:     return index;
770: }

772: // Measure a fit slot and report FIT_CHANGED when the derived index changes.
773: void reportFit(uint32_t id, double width) {
774:     auto it = g.fit_queries.find(id);
775:     if (it == g.fit_queries.end() || !g.bridge) {
776:         return;
777:     }
778:     const int index = deriveFitIndex(it->second, width);
779:     auto prev = g.fit_index.find(id);
780:     if (prev != g.fit_index.end() && prev->second == index) {
781:         return;
782:     }
783:     g.fit_index[id] = index;
784:     g.bridge->fitChanged(id, index);
785: }

883: // Pathland cross-axis alignment (0=Start,1=Center,2=End,3=Fill) applied to a
884: // stack's children via the Layout attached properties: Fill stretches the child
885: // on the stack's cross axis; Start/Center/End set the Layout alignment.
886: void applyStackAlignment(uint32_t parentId, QQuickItem *child) {
887:     if (!child) {
888:         return;
889:     }
890:     auto it = g.stack_align.find(parentId);
891:     if (it == g.stack_align.end()) {
892:         return;
893:     }
894:     const uint16_t comp = g.components[parentId];
895:     const bool vertical = comp == PL_COMP_VSTACK || comp == PL_COMP_LAZY_VSTACK;
896:     const float raw = f32(it->second);
897:     const int idx = (std::isfinite(raw) && std::floor(raw) == raw && raw >= 0.0f && raw <= 3.0f)
898:                         ? static_cast<int>(raw)
899:                         : static_cast<int>(it->second & 0xFF);
900:     QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(child);
901:     if (!a) {
902:         return;
903:     }
904:     if (idx == 3) { // Fill -> stretch on the cross axis
905:         if (vertical) {
906:             a->setFillWidth(true);
907:         } else {
908:             a->setFillHeight(true);
909:         }
910:         return;
911:     }
912:     Qt::Alignment align;
913:     if (vertical) { // Column: cross axis is horizontal
914:         align = idx == 0 ? Qt::AlignLeft : (idx == 1 ? Qt::AlignHCenter : Qt::AlignRight);
915:     } else { // Row: cross axis is vertical
916:         align = idx == 0 ? Qt::AlignTop : (idx == 1 ? Qt::AlignVCenter : Qt::AlignBottom);
917:     }
918:     a->setAlignment(align);
919: }

923:     for (uint32_t childId : g.children_of[parentId]) {
924:         applyStackAlignment(parentId, findWidget(childId));
925:     }
926: }

929: // navigation container, and StackView's push/pop are QML-callable-only (not
930: // invokable from C++ via QMetaObject), so the renderer manages its page cache
931: // itself: pages are children of this Item, only the top is visible.

933:     return createComponent(g.engine, parent, "import QtQuick 2.15\nItem { clip: true }");

936: // Promote a slot's stack wrapper to the nav container (first non-empty ROUTE).
937: // The diff inserts the destination before ROUTE arrives, so the wrapper's inner
938: // layout may already own the destination — detach it (and the layout) before the
939: // swap so the app-owned destination survives the wrapper's deletion.
940: void promoteNavSlot(uint32_t slotId) {
941:     auto it = g.widgets.find(slotId);
942:     if (it == g.widgets.end()) {
943:         return;
944:     }
945:     QQuickItem *old = it->second;
946:     QQuickItem *container = createNavContainer(old->parentItem());
947:     if (!container) {
948:         return;
949:     }
950:     // Fill the slot's parent when it is a plain container (a positioner like
951:     // Row/Column rejects anchors on its children and sizes them itself).
952:     if (old->parentItem() && !isPositioner(old->parentItem())) {
953:         QObject *anchors = container->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
954:         if (anchors) {
955:             anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(old->parentItem()));
956:         }
957:     }
958:     for (QQuickItem *kid : old->childItems()) {
959:         const auto grandkids = kid->childItems();
960:         for (QQuickItem *gk : grandkids) {
961:             gk->setParentItem(nullptr);
962:         }
963:         g.pending_fill.erase(kid);
964:         kid->setParentItem(nullptr);
965:         kid->deleteLater();
966:     }
967:     g.pending_fill.erase(old);
968:     g.widgets[slotId] = container;
969:     g.nav_slots.insert(slotId);
970:     g.nav_stacks[slotId] = container;
971:     old->deleteLater();
972: }

1521:     case PL_PROP_ACTION_ID:

1525:     case PL_PROP_CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS:

1528:     case PL_PROP_BACKGROUND: {
1529:         // A Rectangle-backed node is its own fill; a container gets a background
1530:         // Rectangle behind its content (CSS background).
1531:         QQuickItem *target =
1532:             item->property("radius").isValid() ? item : ensureBackground(id, item);

1546:         if (prop == PL_PROP_BORDER_RADIUS) {

1570:         if (item->property("fillMode").isValid()) {

1572:                               f32(value) >= 0.5f ? 2 /* PreserveAspectCrop */
1573:                                                  : 1 /* PreserveAspectFit */);

1575:         break;

1588:     case PL_PROP_IDEAL_HEIGHT:

1634:     case PL_PROP_MEDIA_LOOP:
1635:         if (QObject *player = mediaPlayerFor(id)) {

1637:         }

1639:     case PL_PROP_MEDIA_RATE:

1658: void applyStringProperty(uint32_t id, uint16_t prop, const char *str, uint32_t len) {
1659:     QQuickItem *item = findWidget(id);
1660:     if (!item) {
1661:         return;
1662:     }
1663:     const QString value = QString::fromUtf8(str, static_cast<int>(len));
1664:     switch (prop) {
1665:     case PL_PROP_FIT_QUERY: {
1666:         std::vector<double> thresholds;
1667:         for (const QString &part : value.split(',', Qt::SkipEmptyParts)) {
1668:             bool ok = false;
1669:             const double v = part.trimmed().toDouble(&ok);
1670:             if (ok) {
1671:                 thresholds.push_back(v);
1672:             }
1673:         }
1674:         g.fit_queries[id] = thresholds;
1675:         g.fit_index.erase(id);
1676:         reportFit(id, item->width());
1677:         break;
1678:     }
1679:     case PL_PROP_ICON_NAME:
1680:         item->setProperty("text", iconGlyph(value));
1681:         break;
1682:     case PL_PROP_MEDIA_SOURCE:
1683:         if (QObject *player = mediaPlayerFor(id)) {
1684:             player->setProperty("source", resolveAsset(value, g.asset_root));
1685:             // Re-apply the app's declared transport state: a play() that landed
1686:             // before the source was known would otherwise stay silent.
1687:             auto st = g.media_play_state.find(id);
1688:             if (st != g.media_play_state.end()) {
1689:                 QMetaObject::invokeMethod(player, st->second != 0 ? "play" : "pause");
1690:             }
1691:         }
1692:         break;
1693:     case PL_PROP_IMAGE_SOURCE:
1694:         item->setProperty("source", resolveAsset(value, g.asset_root));
1695:         break;
1696:     case PL_PROP_FONT_FAMILY: {
1697:         QVariant fv = item->property("font");
1698:         QFont font = fv.value<QFont>();
1699:         font.setFamily(value);
1700:         item->setProperty("font", QVariant::fromValue(font));
1701:         break;

1703:     case PL_PROP_PROMPT:
1704:     case PL_PROP_LABEL:

1707:     case PL_PROP_ROUTE:
1708:         g.nav_route[id] = value;
1709:         // Promote a stack slot to a StackView on the first non-empty ROUTE.
1710:         if (!value.isEmpty() && !g.nav_slots.count(id) && isStackComponent(g.components[id])) {
1711:             promoteNavSlot(id);
1712:         }
1713:         reconcileNav(id);

1715:     default:
1716:         break;

1720: // Reset renderer-owned style to defaults (spec: the renderer owns defaults).
1721: // Value props (VALUE/checked/from/to) are app-owned and left untouched, so a
1722: // slider drag / toggle doesn't lose its position on echo updates.
1723: void resetNode(uint32_t id) {
1724:     QQuickItem *item = findWidget(id);
1725:     if (!item) {
1726:         return;
1727:     }
1728:     // Listener overlays are renderer-owned; the full property set that follows
1729:     // RESET re-attaches them from the (re-sent) EVENT_LISTENERS value.
1730:     detachPointerArea(id);
1731:     g.fg_colors.erase(id);
1732:     g.fg_own.erase(id);
1733:     if (isTextual(item)) {
1734:         uint32_t inherited = 0;
1735:         item->setProperty("color", inheritedForeground(id, &inherited)
1736:                                        ? QColor::fromRgba(inherited)
1737:                                        : QColor(Qt::black));
1738:     } else {
1739:         uint32_t inherited = 0;
1740:         const bool have = inheritedForeground(id, &inherited);
1741:         applyForegroundDescendants(id, have, inherited);
1742:     }
1743:     g.stack_align.erase(id);
1744:     item->setProperty("opacity", 1.0);
1745:     item->setProperty("visible", true);
1746:     if (QQuickItem *lay = layoutOf(item)) {
1747:         lay->setProperty("spacing", 0.0);
1748:         QObject *anchors = lay->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
1749:         if (anchors) {
1750:             anchors->setProperty("margins", 0.0);
1751:             anchors->setProperty("topMargin", 0.0);
1752:             anchors->setProperty("rightMargin", 0.0);
1753:             anchors->setProperty("bottomMargin", 0.0);
1754:             anchors->setProperty("leftMargin", 0.0);
1755:         }
1756:         const auto kids = lay->childItems();
1757:         for (QQuickItem *k : kids) {
1758:             if (QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(k)) {
1759:                 a->setFillWidth(false);
1760:                 a->setFillHeight(false);
1761:                 a->setPreferredWidth(-1);
1762:                 a->setPreferredHeight(-1);
1763:             }
1764:         }
1765:     }
1766:     // Reset the renderer-owned background/border layer.
1767:     QQuickItem *bg = childItemNamed(item, QStringLiteral("pl%1bg").arg(id));
1768:     if (!bg && item->property("radius").isValid()) {
1769:         bg = item;
1770:     }
1771:     if (bg) {
1772:         bg->setProperty("color", QColor(Qt::transparent));
1773:         bg->setProperty("radius", 0.0);
1774:         if (QObject *border = bg->property("border").value<QObject *>()) {
1775:             border->setProperty("width", 0);
1776:         }
1777:     }
1778:     g.shadow_color.erase(id);
1779:     g.shadow_radius.erase(id);
1780:     g.shadow_dx.erase(id);
1781:     g.shadow_dy.erase(id);
1782:     if (QQuickItem *sh = childItemNamed(item, QStringLiteral("pl%1shadow").arg(id))) {
1783:         sh->setProperty("color", QColor(Qt::transparent));
1784:     }
1785: }

1805: void insertChild(uint32_t parentId, uint32_t childId, uint32_t index) {
1806:     QQuickItem *child = findWidget(childId);
1807:     if (!child) {
1808:         return;
1809:     }
1810:     g.parents[childId] = parentId;
1811:     // Maintain the ordered structural mirror for every parent.
1812:     auto &siblings = g.children_of[parentId];
1813:     siblings.erase(std::remove(siblings.begin(), siblings.end(), childId), siblings.end());
1814:     if (index == UINT32_MAX || index >= siblings.size()) {
1815:         siblings.push_back(childId);
1816:     } else {
1817:         siblings.insert(siblings.begin() + index, childId);
1818:     }
1819: 
1820:     if (isNonVisual(g.components[childId])) {
1821:         // Layout-transparent: it exists (owns playback), but no visual slot.
1822:         // CREATE_NODE parented it to the content item as a placeholder; detach.
1823:         if (QQuickItem *nv = findWidget(childId)) {
1824:             nv->setParentItem(nullptr);
1825:         }
1826:         return;
1827:     }
1828:     if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
1829:         rebuildPickerModel(parentId); // options drive the model, not the visual tree
1830:         return;
1831:     }
1832:     if (g.nav_slots.count(parentId)) {
1833:         reconcileNav(parentId); // destination subtree swap -> refresh/replace the top page
1834:         return; // the destination is placed by the nav adapter, not visually here
1835:     }
1836: 
1837:     // GRID_ROW (spec/PRIMITIVES.md): a row's cells are flattened into the parent
1838:     // Grid so columns align across rows. The row itself renders nothing.
1839:     if (g.components[childId] == PL_COMP_GRID_ROW &&
1840:         g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_GRID) {
1841:         g.grid_of[childId] = parentId;
1842:         if (QQuickItem *row = findWidget(childId)) {
1843:             QQuickItem *grid = findWidget(parentId);
1844:             for (QQuickItem *cell : row->childItems()) {
1845:                 cell->setParentItem(grid); // cells already present join the grid
1846:             }
1847:             row->setParentItem(nullptr);
1848:         }
1849:         return;
1850:     }
1851: 
1852:     // A GRID_ROW's cell attaches to the row's grid (flattened), at its global
1853:     // row-major cell index.
1854:     uint32_t visualParentId = parentId;
1855:     uint32_t visualIndex = index;
1856:     if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_GRID_ROW) {
1857:         auto git = g.grid_of.find(parentId);
1858:         if (git != g.grid_of.end()) {
1859:             visualParentId = git->second;
1860:             int n = 0;
1861:             for (uint32_t c : g.children_of[visualParentId]) {
1862:                 if (c == parentId) {
1863:                     break;
1864:                 }
1865:                 n += (g.components[c] == PL_COMP_GRID_ROW)
1866:                          ? static_cast<int>(g.children_of[c].size())
1867:                          : 1;
1868:             }
1869:             const auto &rowKids = g.children_of[parentId];
1870:             auto lit = std::find(rowKids.begin(), rowKids.end(), childId);
1871:             const int local = (lit == rowKids.end()) ? 0 : static_cast<int>(lit - rowKids.begin());
1872:             visualIndex = static_cast<uint32_t>(n + local);
1873:         }
1874:     }
1875: 
1876:     if (g.components[visualParentId] == PL_COMP_BUTTON && !isNonVisual(g.components[childId])) {
1877:         promoteComposite(visualParentId); // children => composite override mode
1878:     }
1879: 
1880:     QQuickItem *parent = findWidget(visualParentId);
1881:     if (!parent) {
1882:         return;
1883:     }
1884:     // Stacks attach children to their inner layout (so `Layout` stretch works);
1885:     // a ScrollView attaches to its contentItem (so content sizes/scrolls it).
1886:     QQuickItem *attach = parent;
1887:     if (isStackComponent(g.components[visualParentId]) || g.composite.count(visualParentId)) {
1888:         attach = layoutOf(parent);
1889:         if (!attach) {
1890:             attach = parent;
1891:         }
1892:     } else if (g.components[visualParentId] == PL_COMP_SCROLL) {
1893:         QVariant ci = parent->property("contentItem");
1894:         if (ci.isValid()) {
1895:             if (QQuickItem *c = ci.value<QQuickItem *>()) {
1896:                 attach = c;
1897:             }
1898:         }
1899:     }
1900: 
1901:     child->setParentItem(attach);
1902:     // Window content (pseudo-parent 0): roots fill the window (GTK's window
1903:     // child expands).
1904:     if (parentId == 0) {
1905:         QObject *anchors = child->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
1906:         if (anchors) {
1907:             anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(g.root));
1908:         }
1909:     }
1910:     applyStackAlignment(parentId, child);
1911:     // Default stack alignment is stretch (CSS `align-items:stretch`): with no
1912:     // explicit ALIGNMENT, a child fills the container's cross axis.
1913:     if (isContainer(visualParentId) && isLayout(attach) &&
1914:         !g.stack_align.count(visualParentId)) {
1915:         if (QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(child)) {
1916:             if (isVerticalContainer(visualParentId)) {
1917:                 a->setFillWidth(true);
1918:             } else {
1919:                 a->setFillHeight(true);
1920:             }
1921:         }
1922:     }
1923:     // A Spacer expands along the container's main axis.
1924:     if (g.components[childId] == PL_COMP_SPACER && isContainer(visualParentId) &&
1925:         isLayout(attach)) {
1926:         if (QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(child)) {
1927:             if (isVerticalContainer(visualParentId)) {
1928:                 a->setFillHeight(true);
1929:             } else {
1930:                 a->setFillWidth(true);
1931:             }
1932:         }
1933:     }
1934:     // A ScrollView fills its parent by default (GTK: halign/valign = Fill), so a
1935:     // scroll content area stretches instead of collapsing to its content. A
1936:     // SIZE_THAT_FITS slot is likewise greedy on both axes (spec/LAYOUT.md).
1937:     if (g.components[childId] == PL_COMP_SCROLL ||
1938:         g.components[childId] == PL_COMP_SIZE_THAT_FITS) {
1939:         if (isLayout(attach)) {
1940:             QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(child);
1941:             if (a) {
1942:                 a->setFillWidth(true);
1943:                 a->setFillHeight(true);
1944:             }
1945:         } else if (!isPositioner(attach)) {
1946:             QObject *anchors = child->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
1947:             if (anchors) {
1948:                 anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(attach));
1949:             }
1950:         }
1951:     }
1952:     // Inherit a container's foreground color (CSS `color` inheritance).
1953:     if (isTextual(child) && !g.fg_own.count(childId)) {
1954:         uint32_t color = 0;
1955:         if (inheritedForeground(childId, &color)) {
1956:             child->setProperty("color", QColor::fromRgba(color));
1957:         }
1958:     }
1959:     // A fit slot's one selected child occupies the whole slot.
1960:     if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_SIZE_THAT_FITS) {
1961:         QObject *anchors = child->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
1962:         if (anchors) {
1963:             anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(attach));
1964:         }
1965:     }
1966:     flushFill(child, attach);
1967:     if (visualIndex == UINT32_MAX) {
1968:         return; // append (already last)
1969:     }
1970:     QList<QQuickItem *> siblingsList = attach->childItems();
1971:     siblingsList.removeAll(child);
1972:     if (static_cast<int>(visualIndex) < siblingsList.size()) {
1973:         QQuickItem *after = siblingsList.at(static_cast<int>(visualIndex));
1974:         if (after != child) {
1975:             child->stackBefore(after);
1976:         }
1977:     }
1978: }
