2024: // Native back: Escape is a platform back request (global, never node-keyed),
2025: // matching the GTK renderer's window-level key controller. BackSpace is
2026: // deferred (needs text-focus detection).
2027: class KeyFilter : public QObject {
2028: public:
2029:     using QObject::QObject;
2030: protected:
2031:     bool eventFilter(QObject *obj, QEvent *ev) override {
2032:         if (ev->type() != QEvent::KeyPress && ev->type() != QEvent::KeyRelease) {
2033:             return QObject::eventFilter(obj, ev);
2034:         }
2035:         auto *ke = static_cast<QKeyEvent *>(ev);
2036:         const bool down = ev->type() == QEvent::KeyPress;
2037:         // Escape is always native back (global, never node-keyed).
2038:         if (down && ke->key() == Qt::Key_Escape) {
2039:             if (g.bridge) {
2040:                 g.bridge->navigateBack();
2041:             }
2042:             return true;
2043:         }
2044:         // BackSpace is native back unless a text input owns the key.
2045:         if (down && ke->key() == Qt::Key_Backspace && !isTextInput(g.focused_component)) {
2046:             if (g.bridge) {

2049:             return true;

2051:         // Report KEY_DOWN/KEY_UP for the focused node (gated by its listener bits
2052:         // inside the Bridge); the event still reaches the focused control.
2053:         if (g.focused_id != 0 && g.bridge) {
2054:             g.bridge->key(g.focused_id, ke->key(), modifierMask(ke->modifiers()),
2055:                           ke->isAutoRepeat(), down);
2056:         }

2075: int pathland_qt_layer_init(PathlandQtWake wake, PathlandQtTick tick,
2076:                            PathlandQtEventFn event_fn, void *user) {
2077:     Q_UNUSED(wake); // reserved: the shell only wakes on run (the host drains the ring)
2078:     if (g.initialized) {
2079:         return 0;
2080:     }
2081:     static int argc = 1;
2082:     static char arg0[] = "pathland-qt";
2083:     static char *argv[] = {arg0, nullptr};
2084:     if (!init_app(argc, argv)) {
2085:         return -1;
2086:     }
2087: 
2088:     g.bridge = new Bridge(g.app);
2089:     g.bridge->event_fn = event_fn;
2090:     g.bridge->user = user;
2091:     g.bridge->gated = &g.gated_ids;
2092:     g.bridge->listeners = &g.node_listeners;
2093:     g.bridge->suppress = &g.suppress;
2094: 
2095:     g.engine = new QQmlEngine(g.app);
2096:     // Qt adds the executable's directory to QML's implicit import path. A
2097:     // `cargo test` binary lives in `target/debug/deps`, which can hold tens of
2098:     // thousands of files; resolving a QML plugin then scans that directory and
2099:     // can take minutes (the headless-test "hang"). We ship no QML there, so
2100:     // drop it and keep only the genuine Qt import paths.
2101:     {
2102:         QStringList imports = g.engine->importPathList();
2103:         imports.removeAll(QCoreApplication::applicationDirPath());
2104:         g.engine->setImportPathList(imports);
2105:     }
2106:     g.engine->rootContext()->setContextProperty("bridge", g.bridge);
2107: 
2108:     g.window = new QQuickWindow();
2109:     g.window->setTitle(QString::fromUtf8("Pathland"));
2110:     g.window->resize(420, 220);
2111:     g.root = g.window->contentItem();
2112: 
2113:     // Native back: Escape on the window is a global back request (see KeyFilter).
2114:     g.window->installEventFilter(new KeyFilter(g.window));
2115: 
2116:     // Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md): the renderer derives the
2117:     // effective scheme from the platform and re-resolves tokens when it
2118:     // changes. Scheme is never carried by the protocol.
2119:     QObject::connect(g.app->styleHints(), &QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged, g.app,
2120:                      []() { reportScheme(); });
2121:     reportScheme();
2122: 
2123:     // Idle tick: pump the ring on the Qt main thread between frames, like the
2124:     // GTK renderer's glib idle pump.
2125:     g.tick_timer = new QTimer(g.app);
2126:     g.tick_timer->setInterval(0);
2127:     g.tick_timer->setSingleShot(false);
2128:     QObject::connect(g.tick_timer, &QTimer::timeout, g.app, [tick, user]() {
2129:         if (tick) {
2130:             tick(user);
2131:         }
2132:     });
2133: 
2134:     g.initialized = true;
2135:     return 0;
2136: }

2138: int pathland_qt_layer_run(const char *title, int width, int height,
2139:                           PathlandQtWake wake, PathlandQtTick tick,
2140:                           PathlandQtEventFn event_fn, void *user) {
2141:     if (pathland_qt_layer_init(wake, tick, event_fn, user) != 0) {
2142:         return -1;

2156: void pathland_qt_layer_apply(const PathlandQtCommand *cmds, uint32_t count) {
2157:     if (!g.initialized || !cmds || count == 0) {
2158:         return;
2159:     }
2160:     for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
2161:         const PathlandQtCommand &c = cmds[i];
2162:         switch (c.kind) {
2163:         case PLQT_CREATE_NODE: {
2164:             const uint16_t component = static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b & 0xFFFF);
2165:             QQuickItem *item = createComponent(g.engine, g.root, qmlFor(component, c.a).toUtf8());
2166:             if (item) {
2167:                 g.widgets[c.a] = item;
2168:                 g.components[c.a] = component;
2169:                 if (component == PL_COMP_SIZE_THAT_FITS) {
2170:                     const uint32_t id = c.a;
2171:                     QObject::connect(item, &QQuickItem::widthChanged, item,
2172:                                      [id, item]() { reportFit(id, item->width()); });
2173:                 }
2174:                 if (isTextInput(component)) {
2175:                     const uint32_t id = c.a;
2176:                     QObject::connect(item, &QQuickItem::activeFocusChanged, item, [id, item]() {
2177:                         const bool focused = item->hasActiveFocus();
2178:                         if (focused) {
2179:                             g.focused_id = id;
2180:                             g.focused_component = g.components[id];
2181:                         } else if (g.focused_id == id) {
2182:                             g.focused_id = 0;
2183:                             g.focused_component = 0;
2184:                         }
2185:                         if (g.bridge) {
2186:                             g.bridge->focusChanged(id, focused);
2187:                             g.bridge->editingChanged(id, focused);
2188:                         }
2189:                     });
2190:                 }
2191:             }
2192:             break;
2193:         }
2194:         case PLQT_DELETE_NODE:
2195:             deleteNode(c.a);
2196:             break;
2197:         case PLQT_INSERT_CHILD:
2198:             insertChild(c.a, c.b, c.c);
2199:             break;
2200:         case PLQT_REMOVE_CHILD: {
2201:             const uint32_t parentId = c.a;
2202:             const uint32_t childId = c.b;
2203:             g.parents.erase(childId);
2204:             auto &siblings = g.children_of[parentId];
2205:             siblings.erase(std::remove(siblings.begin(), siblings.end(), childId), siblings.end());
2206:             if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
2207:                 rebuildPickerModel(parentId);
2208:             } else if (g.nav_slots.count(parentId)) {
2209:                 reconcileNav(parentId);
2210:             } else {
2211:                 QQuickItem *child = findWidget(childId);
2212:                 if (child) {
2213:                     child->setParentItem(nullptr); // keep alive (may be reinserted)
2214:                 }
2215:             }
2216:             break;
2217:         }
2218:         case PLQT_MOVE_CHILD:
2219:             insertChild(c.a, c.b, c.c); // reorder == reinsert at index
2220:             break;
2221:         case PLQT_SET_TEXT: {
2222:             QQuickItem *item = findWidget(c.a);
2223:             if (item && c.str) {
2224:                 g.suppress = true;
2225:                 item->setProperty("text", QString::fromUtf8(c.str, static_cast<int>(c.str_len)));
2226:                 g.suppress = false;
2227:             }
2228:             // A picker option's label feeds its parent's ComboBox model.
2229:             auto pit = g.parents.find(c.a);
2230:             if (pit != g.parents.end() && g.components[pit->second] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
2231:                 rebuildPickerModel(pit->second);
2232:             }
2233:             // Record for the test hook.
2234:             if (c.str && c.str_len > 0) {
2235:                 const uint32_t n = c.str_len < sizeof(g.last_text) - 1 ? c.str_len
2236:                                                                        : sizeof(g.last_text) - 1;
2237:                 std::memcpy(g.last_text, c.str, n);
2238:                 g.last_text[n] = '\0';
2239:                 g.last_text_len = n;
2240:             }
2241:             break;
2242:         }
2243:         case PLQT_SET_PROPERTY: {
2244:             const uint16_t prop = static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b & 0xFFFF);
2245:             const uint8_t vt = static_cast<uint8_t>((c.b >> 16) & 0xFF);
2246:             g.suppress = true;
2247:             applyProperty(c.a, prop, vt, c.c);
2248:             g.suppress = false;
2249:             break;
2250:         }
2251:         case PLQT_SET_STRING_PROPERTY:
2252:             g.suppress = true;
2253:             applyStringProperty(c.a, static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b), c.str, c.str_len);
2254:             g.suppress = false;
2255:             break;
2256:         case PLQT_RESET_NODE:
2257:             resetNode(c.a);
2258:             break;
2259:         case PLQT_SET_SCHEME:
2260:             break; // MVP: scheme handling is a follow-up
2261:         case PLQT_SET_DATE: {
2262:             // A DATE_PICKER value: days since the Unix epoch + millis of day.
2263:             // The renderer owns the formatting (QML approximation of a picker).
2264:             if (QQuickItem *item = findWidget(c.a)) {
2265:                 const qint64 days = static_cast<int32_t>(c.b);
2266:                 const QDate date = QDate(1970, 1, 1).addDays(days);
2267:                 QString text = date.toString(QStringLiteral("yyyy-MM-dd"));
2268:                 const int millis = static_cast<int>(c.c);
2269:                 if (millis > 0) {
2270:                     const int hours = millis / 3'600'000;
2271:                     const int minutes = (millis / 60'000) % 60;
2272:                     text += QStringLiteral(" %1:%2")
2273:                                 .arg(hours, 2, 10, QChar('0'))
2274:                                 .arg(minutes, 2, 10, QChar('0'));
2275:                 }
2276:                 g.suppress = true;
2277:                 item->setProperty("text", text);
2278:                 g.suppress = false;
2279:             }
2280:             break;
2281:         }
2282:         }
2283:     }
2284:     g.apply_count += count;
2285: }

1: //! C ABI for the Pathland Qt renderer (foreign hosts, e.g. Java via JNA).
2: //!
3: //! Mirrors `pathland-render-gtk`'s `capi.rs`:
4: //! - `pathland_qt_run(host, on_event)` — pump a `pathland-view-native`
5: //!   `NativeHost`'s ring in-process.
6: //! - `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` — pump a
7: //!   `libpathland_core` ring borrowed in-process (the route for hosts that
8: //!   emit opcodes themselves, e.g. the Java DSL's `RingOpcodeSink`).
9: //!
10: //! Both block until the Qt event loop exits and pass a bare program name to
11: //! Qt (the process argv belongs to the embedding host — e.g. a JVM's `-cp` /
12: //! `-D` flags — and must not be parsed as Qt options).
13: 
14: use std::ffi::{c_char, c_void, CStr};
15: 
16: use pathland_core::Event;
17: use pathland_core_transport::{
18:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, RingTransport, TransportError,
19: };
20: use pathland_native::NativeHost;
21: 
22: use crate::run::{run_with_pump_sized, EventCallback, Pump};
23: 
24: /// A `Pump` over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost` owned by the foreign host.
25: struct NativeHostHandle(*mut NativeHost);
26: 
27: impl Pump for NativeHostHandle {
28:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
29:         // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); the host must not destroy
30:         // the host until `pathland_qt_run` returns.
31:         unsafe { FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *self.0) }
32:     }
33: 
34:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
35:         // SAFETY: as above.
36:         unsafe { DriverTransport::send_input(&mut *self.0, event) }
37:     }
38: }
39: 
40: /// A `Pump` over a `libpathland_core` `RingTransport` borrowed from the foreign
41: /// host. Same contract as [`NativeHostHandle`].
42: struct CoreRingHandle(*mut RingTransport);
43: 
44: impl Pump for CoreRingHandle {
45:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
46:         // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); the ring outlives the call.
47:         unsafe { FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *self.0) }
48:     }
49: 
50:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
51:         // SAFETY: as above.
52:         unsafe { DriverTransport::send_input(&mut *self.0, event) }
53:     }
54: }
55: 
56: /// Run the Qt renderer over a `pathland-view-native` host's shared ring.
57: ///
58: /// `host` is the opaque handle from `pathland_native_create`; the renderer
59: /// pumps its ring in-process (frames in, events out). `on_event` is called
60: /// (on the Qt main thread, with no payload) whenever a raw input was written;
61: /// the host then drains the event ring via `pathland_native_drain_events` and
62: /// may re-enter `pathland_native_*` to update the tree and re-emit.
63: ///
64: /// Blocks until the Qt event loop exits (window closed).
65: #[no_mangle]
66: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_qt_run(host: *mut c_void, on_event: Option<EventCallback>) {
67:     if host.is_null() {
68:         return;
69:     }
70:     let pump: Box<dyn Pump> = Box::new(NativeHostHandle(host as *mut NativeHost));
71:     run_with_pump_sized("Pathland Qt Demo", pump, on_event, 420, 220);
72: }

75: ///
76: /// `ring` is the pointer from `pathland_core_ring_mut` (the underlying
77: /// `RingTransport` of a `pathland_core_create` handle). This is the route for
78: /// hosts that emit opcodes themselves — no `pathland-view-native` host is
79: /// involved. `width`/`height` size the default window (0 = renderer default).
80: /// Blocks until the Qt event loop exits.
81: #[no_mangle]
82: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_qt_run_ring(
83:     ring: *mut c_void,
84:     on_event: Option<EventCallback>,
85:     width: u32,
86:     height: u32,
87: ) {
88:     if ring.is_null() {
89:         return;
90:     }
91:     let pump: Box<dyn Pump> = Box::new(CoreRingHandle(ring as *mut RingTransport));
92:     run_with_pump_sized(
93:         "Pathland Qt Demo",
94:         pump,
95:         on_event,
96:         width.max(1) as i32,
97:         height.max(1) as i32,
98:     );
99: }

102: /// resolve against a directory extracted by the host (mirrors

===================================================================
--- lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/status.md	
+++ lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/status.md	
@@ -1,267 +1,270 @@
 # pathland-render-qt — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 20, 2026
 
 The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
 scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
 
 **Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
 - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
   **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
 - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative qtmultimedia`).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
   `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
   core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
 - **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
   `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
   set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
   `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
 - **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
   emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
   commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
   preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
   renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
   clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
   are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
   `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
 - **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
   `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
   `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
   padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
   `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView` (content attaches to its
   `contentItem`; fills its parent by default), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
   unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
   `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
   → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
   handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
   activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
   (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
   `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
   (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
   `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
   native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
   (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
   FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
   `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family via the `font` `QFont`
   property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible, z,
   value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
   `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
   prompt/label→placeholder, image source. **Stack alignment**: a stack's
   `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
   (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).
   **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
   `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
   slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
 - **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
   *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
   attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
   the create-time contentItem placeholder.
 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
   (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
   `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
   ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
   `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
 - **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
   is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
   its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
   Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
   spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
   `DELETE`.
 - **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
   `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
   renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
 - **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
   fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
   shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
   concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
   init.
 - **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
   `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
   C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
 - **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
   an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
   idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
 - **Asset root** (`pathland_qt_set_asset_root` /
   `pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root`): web-style `/_pathland/...` image/media
   sources resolve against a host-extracted local directory (the Qt analogue of
   `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); the Java Qt host extracts `DemoAssets` and
   sets it before `runRing`.
 - **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
   on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
   `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
   `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
   a bare program name to Qt.
 - **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
   shared ring).
 
 - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
   **Page sizing:** each page wrapper is anchored to fill the nav container
   (`placeDestination`), so the header/content/destination chain is sized and the
   destination subtree fills the content area (previously the page wrapper was
   attached unsized, collapsing the content to 0×0 and showing only an
   overflowing title).
 
 - **Post-merge protocol parity (October 2026)**: the crate was merged onto the
   shared `PARAMETER` rename and now maps the protocol surface added on `main`:
   - `ICON` (0x0B) → a `Text` item whose glyph is resolved from `ICON_NAME` by a
     renderer-owned canonical-name map (unknown names fall back to a dot), with
     `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE` reuse (spec/ICONS.md).
   - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) → **non-visual** (layout-transparent: created but
     never attached) hosting a QML `MediaPlayer` + `AudioOutput`
     (spec/MEDIA.md).
   - `VIDEO` (0x0A) → a `VideoOutput` surface; `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` binds its
     `source` to the referenced controller's `MediaPlayer` (a reference, not a
     parent/child edge).
   - `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) → a transparent vertical container.
   - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` (0x17) → a greedy two-axis slot; its one selected child
     fills it.
   - `GRID_ROW` (0x1D) → a row-grouping container whose cells flatten into
     the parent Grid.
 - **Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core`): `LIST`-typed properties
   (`FIT_QUERY`) decode into `HostNode::lists`, and `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` into
   `HostNode::date` — so the Qt layer can measure fit slots and format dates.
 - **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit measurement**: the slot's `FIT_QUERY` thresholds reach
   the C++ layer as CSV; a width change derives the fit index (largest
   `minWidth` ≤ allocated width) and reports `FIT_CHANGED` (only when it
   changes).
 - **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: a row's cells attach directly to the parent Grid
   (row-major), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.
 - **`DATE_PICKER`**: `SET_DATE` (days since epoch + millis of day) renders as an
   ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field — a QML approximation
   (Qt Quick has no native date picker).
 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md): pointer `hover`/`leave` (`POINTER_MOVE`
   hovering/leaving) from the listener `MouseArea`; `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the
   focused text input (component-type/key-listener gated); `FOCUS_CHANGED` /
   `EDITING_CHANGED` / `SUBMIT` for text inputs (gated by the matching
   `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits); BackSpace is native back unless a text input is
   focused (focus-aware, no longer deferred).
 - **Visual styling layer** (parity with the web/GTK demos):
   - `BACKGROUND_COLOR` / `BORDER_*` / `BORDER_RADIUS` render on a background
     `Rectangle` behind a container's content (stacks reuse an injected
     `pl<id>bg`; plain containers create one lazily); `Rectangle`-backed nodes
     set them directly. `RESET_NODE` clears them.
   - **Composite control mode** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §2): a `Button` that gains
     children is promoted from the native widget to a bare `Item`+`ColumnLayout`
     shell that renders the app's `ButtonStyle` body, so `PlainButtonStyle` /
     `BorderedButtonStyle` buttons look like the web/GTK ones. Leaf buttons stay
     native.
   - **Foreground inheritance** (CSS `color`): a container's `COLOR` is inherited
     by descendant `Text`/`Icon` that don't set their own.
   - **Layout defaults**: cross-axis stretch (`align-items:stretch`) when no
     `ALIGNMENT` is set; `Spacer` expands on the main axis; `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
   - **`TEXT_STYLE`** applies a base typography (size + weight) that raw
     `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT` override; **`SHADOW_*`** draws a best-effort
     offset shadow layer.
 - **Media transport** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`
   (play/pause), `MEDIA_POSITION` (seek, seconds→ms), `MEDIA_VOLUME` /
   `MEDIA_MUTED` (via `AudioOutput`), `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
   `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
   `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` reports (reported by the
   controller's component type, not gated by `BINDING_ID`; programmatic sets are
   echo-suppressed). A play/pause declared before the source is re-applied when
   the source lands.
 - **Layout/property parity**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_*`,
   `CONTENT_MODE` (image fit/fill), `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_COLOR` /
   `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_RADIUS`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`,
   `TRUNCATION_MODE`, and `GRID_COLUMNS` (via the `Layout` attached properties
   where applicable).
 - **Headless test hang fixed**: Qt adds the executable's directory to QML's
   implicit import path; a `cargo test` binary lives in a huge `target/debug/deps`
   and plugin resolution scanned it for minutes. The shell now drops the
   application directory from the engine's import path at init, so
   `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` completes in ~2s (no copy-to-temp workaround).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **`MENU` popup item list**: Qt 6 has no `MenuButton`; the trigger is a
   `Button` and the action-item popup is not built (documented gap).
 - **`COLOR_PICKER`** remains a `Button` approximation (a QML color-swatch popup
   is a follow-up); `DATE_PICKER` is an ISO-text QML approximation, not a native
   dialog.
 - **`PICKER` option styling** and `SHAPE` path approximation. Native **leaf**
   controls keep Qt Quick Controls' own chrome (background/border); the styling
   layer covers containers, composite controls, and `Rectangle`-backed nodes.
 - **Icons** are renderer-owned glyphs (the canonical `ICON_NAME` → a Unicode
   symbol), not the web's SVG/Lucide set — recognizable but not pixel-identical.
 - **Shadows** are an offset rectangle approximation, not a blurred
   `MultiEffect` shadow.
 - **Keys/events beyond the focused text input**: keys are reported for a focused
   text input; keys on other focused controls, `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, and
   `DATE_CHANGED` are not yet reported. Hover/leave use `POINTER_MOVE` (the
   listener mask bit).
 - **FILL inside plain positioners**: `GRID` (a `QQuickGrid`) rejects
   `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid
   defers and is skipped (the positioner sizes it). Stacks use `RowLayout`/
   `ColumnLayout` so FILL children stretch properly.
 - The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
   does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
   tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
 - The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` (the spec table is aspirational) —
   the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
   vehicle.
 - `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
   intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
 - **Java JNA demo** (`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`) runs the shared
   `SplitNavDemo` (incl. native navigation) via `pathland_qt_run_ring`.
 - Lazy views render eagerly.
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (needs Qt6 dev libs; offscreen for the FFI
 tests) — the delta diff suite, the end-to-end FFI batch
 (`command_batch_crosses_into_cpp_offscreen`), the **full pipeline**
 (`renderer_drives_live_qml_scene`: DSL → engine → frame → shared decode →
 delta diff → FFI → live QML `Column`/`Text`/`Button`/`Slider` with spacing/value
 applied and a delta re-applied), **FILL/Layout stretch**
 (`fill_child_stretches_inside_stack`: FILL → `Layout.fillWidth`, fixed →
 `Layout.preferredWidth`, stack `ALIGNMENT=FILL` stretches the cross axis, root
-anchored to the window), pointer-listener MouseArea attachment
+anchored to the window), **stack geometry** (`vstack_lays_out_children_vertically`
+and `hstack_lays_out_children_horizontally`: a `render_once` layout pass then
+asserts children stack on the main axis, are cross-axis aligned, and the
+`SPACING` gap lands between them), pointer-listener MouseArea attachment
 (`pointer_listeners_attach_mousearea`), the event path
 (`decode_maps_pointer_and_global_events`, `ring_event_writes_pointer_into_ring_and_wakes`,
 `scheme_event_reapplies_without_waking`, `text_event_string_is_length_prefixed`,
 `frame_has_reset_detects_meta_reset`), and Phase-B control coverage
 (`control_widgets_construct_and_apply_props`, `picker_builds_model_from_option_children`),
 and the nav adapter (`nav_slot_promotes_and_pushes_root_page`,
 `nav_depth_push_and_pop`, `nav_replace_same_depth_new_route`,
 `nav_custom_chrome_bare_pages`), plus post-merge parity
 (`new_components_and_media_binding`: ICON glyph resolution, a layout-transparent
 MEDIA_CONTROLLER, and a VIDEO surface bound to its controller) media event
 decoding (`decode_maps_media_reports`), the shared decode parity
 (`decodes_list_and_date_values` in `pathland-render-core`; `list_property_is_forwarded_as_csv`,
 `date_change_is_forwarded_once`), `SIZE_THAT_FITS`
 (`size_that_fits_derives_index_from_width`), `GRID_ROW`
 (`grid_row_flattens_into_the_grid`), `DATE_PICKER`
 (`date_picker_formats_set_date`), and the event family
 (`decode_maps_hover_key_and_focus`), and the visual styling layer
 (`container_background_border_and_radius`, `button_with_child_renders_composite`,
 `foreground_color_inherits_to_text`, `default_stack_stretch_and_spacer`,
 `text_style_and_shadow`). `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` now
 completes directly (the import-path fix). Full workspace: `cd lib/rust && cargo test`.
 Java JNA demo: `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` (headless `RingEventReaderTest`
 runs in the Maven reactor; the live host mounts `SplitNavDemo`).
 Demo: `scripts/run-rust-qt-demo.sh`.

519: ### ZStack — `ZSTACK` 0x12
520: 
521: Depth-overlapping layer stack: children are drawn in depth order — **child index =
522: draw order**, later = on top. An explicit `Z_INDEX` overrides that order: a
523: higher value draws **on top of** lower values, and equal values tie-break by
524: child index (SwiftUI `.zIndex(_:)` parity). **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (enum:
525: `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), plus layout modifiers (Fixed/Fill

527: children occupy the same box by design; there is no gap between them.

529: **Layout & sizing** (SwiftUI `ZStack` / Compose `Box` semantics)
530: 
531: - **Overlay allocation**: unlike a flex stack, children do **not** add to each
532:   other along an axis — they share one box. Each child keeps its own size (a
533:   Fixed box, or a Hug natural size) and is **positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` on
534:   **both axes**; only a **`Fill`-sized child** stretches to the stack's size.
535: - **Own size**: the stack **hugs to its largest child** by default — on each
536:   axis its size is the **maximum** of its children's sizes, never the sum. A
537:   Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
538:   propagation (a `Fill` child on an axis makes the Hug stack `Fill` on that
539:   axis, see the stack layout model above) — expands to the parent's proposal.
540:   `ZStack { Color.red }` fills (Color is layout-greedy); `ZStack { Text("hi") }`
541:   hugs the text.
542: - **Alignment**: `ALIGNMENT` positions each child on **both** axes with a
543:   **2D position code** (SwiftUI `Alignment` / Compose `Alignment` parity) — the
544:   code's horizontal and vertical components place the child within the stack's
545:   box. Position-only: it never resizes a child.
546: 
547:   | code | horizontal | vertical | meaning |
548:   |------|------------|----------|---------|
549:   | `0` | start | start | top-leading |
550:   | `1` | center | center | centered |
551:   | `2` | end | end | bottom-trailing |
552:   | `3` | center | start | top-center |
553:   | `4` | center | end | bottom-center |
554:   | `5` | start | center | center-leading |
555:   | `6` | end | center | center-trailing |
556:   | `7` | end | start | top-trailing |
557:   | `8` | start | end | bottom-leading |

### ZStack — `ZSTACK` 0x12

Depth-overlapping layer stack: children are drawn in depth order — **child index =
draw order**, later = on top. An explicit `Z_INDEX` overrides that order: a
higher value draws **on top of** lower values, and equal values tie-break by
child index (SwiftUI `.zIndex(_:)` parity). **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (enum:
`Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), plus layout modifiers (Fixed/Fill
`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, `PADDING`, `CONTENT_MARGINS` as an inset). **No `SPACING`** —
children occupy the same box by design; there is no gap between them.

**Layout & sizing** (SwiftUI `ZStack` / Compose `Box` semantics)

- **Overlay allocation**: unlike a flex stack, children do **not** add to each
  other along an axis — they share one box. Each child keeps its own size (a
  Fixed box, or a Hug natural size) and is **positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` on
  **both axes**; only a **`Fill`-sized child** stretches to the stack's size.
- **Own size**: the stack **hugs to its largest child** by default — on each
  axis its size is the **maximum** of its children's sizes, never the sum. A
  Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
  propagation (a `Fill` child on an axis makes the Hug stack `Fill` on that
  axis, see the stack layout model above) — expands to the parent's proposal.
  `ZStack { Color.red }` fills (Color is layout-greedy); `ZStack { Text("hi") }`
  hugs the text.
- **Alignment**: `ALIGNMENT` positions each child on **both** axes with a
  **2D position code** (SwiftUI `Alignment` / Compose `Alignment` parity) — the
  code's horizontal and vertical components place the child within the stack's
  box. Position-only: it never resizes a child.

  | code | horizontal | vertical | meaning |
  |------|------------|----------|---------|
  | `0` | start | start | top-leading |
  | `1` | center | center | centered |
  | `2` | end | end | bottom-trailing |
  | `3` | center | start | top-center |
  | `4` | center | end | bottom-center |
  | `5` | start | center | center-leading |
  | `6` | end | center | center-trailing |
  | `7` | end | start | top-trailing |
  | `8` | start | end | bottom-leading |

  `0`/absent is the default (top-leading, Compose `TopStart` parity; SwiftUI
  `ZStack` defaults to `.center`). A **stack** (`VStack`/`HStack`) reads a
  **single axis** of the same code — the `VStack` cross-axis is horizontal
  (`0/1/2` = leading/center/trailing), the `HStack` cross-axis vertical
  (`0/1/2` = top/center/bottom).
- **Overflow**: a Fixed box constrains layout but does not clip — content that
  exceeds it is drawn outside the box unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it
  (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity).
- **Edge cases**: the first child is **not** a special "background" — it follows
  the same size model (a Fixed first child keeps its exact box; a `Fill` one
  stretches); draw order is child index, with an explicit `Z_INDEX` overriding it
  (higher = on top, equal → child index); a `Fill` child in a Hug ZStack
  propagates (fills the parent's proposal).

Static 2D matrix grid, eagerly rendered with aligned rows & columns. Children
are cells, **row-major in insertion order** — child *i* occupies the cell at
`(row = i / columns, column = i % columns)`. **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (a 2D

The spec is rich for ZStack semantics: ALIGNMENT (2D position code), draw order (child index, Z_INDEX override), overlay allocation, hug to largest child, Fill children stretch, etc.

But the Qt renderer's actual implementation of ZStack is minimal: `ZSTACK → Item` (plain Item). Let me verify there's no ZStack alignment handling in applyProperty/insertChild. From my earlier read:

- `applyStackAlignment` handles stacks via `stack_align`, but only for `isVerticalContainer`/`isHorizontalContainer`? Actually `applyStackAlignment` reads `g.components[parentId]` and sets `vertical = comp == VSTACK || LAZY_VSTACK`. For ZStack, vertical=false → treats as horizontal (Row), setting fillHeight or alignment on Layout attached properties. But ZStack children aren't in a layout (ZStack is plain Item, not stack component), so `insertChild` doesn't call applyStackAlignment for ZStack? Let me check: in insertChild, `applyStackAlignment(parentId, child)` is called unconditionally after attach. Let me re-check.

From insertChild code (lines 1901-1922):
```
child->setParentItem(attach);
if (parentId == 0) { anchors.fill root }
applyStackAlignment(parentId, child);   // <-- always called
if (isContainer(visualParentId) && isLayout(attach) && !stack_align.count(...)) { default stretch }
```

So `applyStackAlignment(parentId, child)` is called for ALL parents including ZStack. It checks `g.stack_align.find(parentId)`. If no ALIGNMENT property was set, stack_align has no entry → returns early. So for a ZStack with no ALIGNMENT, nothing happens. Good.

If a ZStack has ALIGNMENT set, `applyProperty` ALIGNMENT does `g.stack_align[id]=value; reapplyStackAlignment(id);` → applies to children via layoutAttached (which creates QQuickLayoutAttached even for non-layout items). That would set fillWidth/fillHeight or Layout.alignment on the child — but since the child's parent is a plain Item (not a layout), the Layout attached properties have no effect. So ZStack alignment is effectively unimplemented in the Qt renderer.

So the current Qt renderer ZStack behavior:
- Plain Item wrapper.
- Children attach directly (overlap at 0,0 by default).
- No alignment, no z-index handling, no hug-to-largest, no Fill propagation. (These are spec gaps.)

What should the test assert? The user wants "test for zstack in qt renderer" ensuring it's "laid out correctly". Given the minimal implementation, the meaningful test is:

1. ZStack children are direct children of the ZStack item (overlapping, not axis-distributed).
2. Children overlap at the same origin (x==0, y==0 by default) — proving depth-stacking rather than axis layout.
3. Possibly draw order (child index) — but Qt draw order is via childItems order, which we could check. Actually the current implementation doesn't do anything special for z-order; children are appended in insertion order, and later siblings render on top by Qt's default. So we can assert child order is preserved (child 2 before child 3 in childItems).

Let me check what test hooks are available: `pathland_qt_layer_widget_child_count(id)`, `pathland_qt_layer_widget_position`, `pathland_qt_layer_widget_size`. For draw order, there's no direct hook, but I could add one, or rely on child ordering via... Actually `widget_child_count` returns the count. There's no hook to get child order/ids. Hmm.

But wait — do I need a z-order hook? The spec says child index = draw order. In Qt, `childItems()` returns in z-order (actually the order they were added / stacking order). For a plain Item with no z manipulation, children render in insertion order (later on top). The current implementation inserts children in order via insertChild and uses `stackBefore` only for explicit index. For ZStack with append (u32::MAX), children append in order.

To test "laid out correctly", the key is: children overlap (same box), not stacked along an axis. The most important and robust assertion:

- Two children (fixed sizes) in a ZStack → both at (0,0) (overlapping), same position, NOT one below/right of the other.

Plus optionally:
- Both are direct children (child count == 2 on the ZStack).

For ZStack children with default alignment, they should be at (0,0). But wait — what about the ZStack's own size? The ZStack is a plain Item. If it's the root, it's anchored to fill (420x220). Children with fixed size sit at (0,0). If a child is a TEXT with no size, it sits at (0,0) with implicit size.

For a robust deterministic test, I'd:
- ZSTACK (id 1) root or nested.
- Two children with fixed sizes (e.g., COLOR/Rectangle nodes, or TEXT with fixed WIDTH/HEIGHT).
- Assert both at x=0,y=0 (overlap) and same position.

Actually, let me reconsider whether children of a plain Item default to (0,0). Yes, a QQuickItem with no anchors and no position has x=0,y=0. When parented to a plain Item, they all sit at (0,0) relative to the parent. So x2==x3==0, y2==y3==0.

But is there value in testing draw order? The current renderer doesn't implement Z_INDEX or explicit z-order for ZStack (it's a spec gap). So I shouldn't test z-order as "correct" because it's not implemented beyond Qt's default. Actually Qt's default: later siblings draw on top. And insertChild appends in order. So child order IS preserved and later = on top, which happens to match the spec's "child index = draw order, later = on top". But there's no hook to verify draw order easily.

Let me keep the test focused and meaningful:
1. ZStack is a plain container: children overlap (same origin) — depth stack, not axis layout.
2. Children are direct children (child count).
3. Verify that unlike VStack/HStack, the second child does NOT shift along an axis (its position equals the first's).

This is a good, faithful test of "laid out correctly" for the current implementation.

However, I should also consider: should I test ZStack alignment? Given the Qt renderer doesn't implement ZStack ALIGNMENT (it's a documented gap?), I shouldn't write a test asserting alignment works — it would fail. Let me verify ZStack alignment is indeed not implemented by checking status.md gaps. The status.md "Not implemented / gaps" section doesn't explicitly mention ZStack alignment. Let me check.

Actually, let me check whether there's a gap listed. From status.md I read earlier, the "Not implemented / gaps" list includes FILL inside plain positioners, MENU popup, COLOR_PICKER, etc. It doesn't explicitly list ZStack alignment as a gap. But the implementation clearly doesn't handle ZStack 2D alignment.

Let me be careful: I should write a test that passes against the current implementation and verifies real behavior. The safest meaningful test: ZStack children overlap (depth stacking) and are direct children, contrasting with VStack/HStack axis layout.

Let me also consider whether I should verify the ZStack "hug to largest child" or "Fill propagation". Those aren't implemented either (ZStack is a plain Item; its size is whatever the parent/anchors give, and as root it's anchored to fill).

Given the implementation, the test should assert the currently-correct behavior: overlap at origin.

Let me now also check: is there any existing ZStack test in the Qt renderer tests? From grep, only my recently-added tests reference component_type::ZSTACK (as a wrapper root). No ZStack-specific test. So this is a new test.

Let me also check the DSL: does the Rust DSL have a `zstack!` macro? Yes (`zstack` mentioned in spec DSL.md line 1279). For the test, I'll use hand-built commands (as the user accepted for HStack/VStack) for deterministic geometry.

Now let me also determine: what's a good component for ZStack children? TEXT with fixed WIDTH/HEIGHT, or COLOR (Rectangle). Using COLOR/Rectangle gives a clean size without text metrics. But TEXT is fine if I set fixed WIDTH/HEIGHT. Actually, to prove overlap cleanly, I'll use two TEXT children with fixed WIDTH and HEIGHT (e.g., 100x50), and assert both are at (0,0).

Wait, but if I want to also show they'd overlap and NOT be axis-distributed, position is enough.

Let me also verify: does a plain Item (ZStack) as root get anchored to fill? Yes, insertChild with parentId==0 anchors fill root. So ZStack root = 420x220. Children at (0,0).

Actually, let me reconsider: should the ZStack be root or nested? For VStack/HStack I used a ZStack root wrapper and nested the stack under test with fixed size. For the ZStack test, I can make the ZStack the root directly (children at 0,0), or nest it. Simpler: ZStack as root, children with fixed size, assert overlap at (0,0).

But there's a subtlety: as root anchored to fill, children at (0,0) with fixed size — good. Their positions (0,0) prove overlap.

Let me also think: should I assert that the ZStack is NOT using a layout (i.e., children are direct children, count == 2, and widget_child_count returns 2)? The `widget_child_count` uses `layoutOf(item)` which returns the inner layout if any; for ZStack (plain Item) there's no layout child, so it returns item's childItems count = 2. Good.

Now, one more consideration: `applyStackAlignment` is called for ZStack children on insert. With no ALIGNMENT property set, `stack_align` is empty, so it returns early. Good — children stay at (0,0).

So the plan:
1. Add one test `zstack_overlaps_children_in_depth_order` (or `zstack_stacks_children_in_depth`) in ffi.rs tests.
2. Use hand-built commands:
   - ZSTACK (id 1) → content item 0 (root, fills window)
   - TEXT (id 2) "A" fixed WIDTH 100, HEIGHT 50
   - TEXT (id 3) "B" fixed WIDTH 100, HEIGHT 50
   - insert 1←2, 1←3
   - render_once
3. Assertions:
   - widget_child_count(1) == 2 (both children direct on the ZStack, no inner layout)
   - position(2) == position(3) == (0,0): x2==x3, y2==y3, and both ≈ 0 (overlap, depth stacking rather than axis layout)
   - size: w2==w3==100, h2==h3==50 (children keep their own size, not stretched/laid out)

Actually, since children are at (0,0) with fixed sizes, I can assert x2==0, y2==0, x3==0, y3==0 exactly. But to be robust to offscreen quirk, use epsilon.

Should I also test draw order? There's no hook for it. I could add a hook to get child order (list of ids under a parent in z-order). But that's more work and z-order isn't explicitly managed. I'll keep it minimal and focus on the core layout semantics: overlap (depth stacking) + direct children + own size preserved.

Hmm, but is "both at (0,0)" a strong enough "laid out correctly" test? It proves ZStack doesn't lay children along an axis. Combined with child count and size preservation, it's a solid test distinguishing ZStack from VStack/HStack.

Alternatively, I could add a comparison: contrast that in a ZStack the second child's position equals the first (overlap), whereas in VStack/HStack the second child shifts. But that's implicit.

Let me also think about whether to verify the z-order/draw order. Given the spec emphasizes "child index = draw order, later = on top", and Qt's default does exactly that (later childItems render on top), it would be nice to verify. But there's no existing hook to query z-order. I'd need to add a hook like `pathland_qt_layer_widget_z(id)` or `pathland_qt_layer_child_order(parent, out)`. 

Actually, Qt's `childItems()` returns children in a specific order. The stacking (z) can be queried via `item->z()` but that's the explicit z property, not stacking order. For siblings without explicit z, the stacking order is the childItems order. There's no simple QQuickItem API to get "stacking order" other than childItems order.

I think for a focused, correct, passing test, I'll cover:
1. Children overlap (depth) — position equal.
2. Direct children (no axis layout).
3. Own size preserved.

I could optionally add a z-order check by adding a test hook that returns the objectName/id of the topmost child, but ids aren't directly available on QML items except via objectName "pl<id>". Actually the widget items have objectName "pl<id>". I could add a hook that returns, for a parent, the objectName of its last child item (which would be on top). But this is more work and arguably over-engineering for "laid out correctly".

Let me keep it minimal and aligned with the previous two tests. I'll present the plan and note the option.

Actually, let me reconsider the scope. The user's previous request was "hstack and vstack laid out correctly". Now "zstack". The natural third test should mirror those: verify ZStack lays children out correctly = depth overlap. I'll mirror the structure.

Let me also double check: does the ZStack renderer maybe need a test that children overlap but a Fill child stretches? That's not implemented. Skip.

Let me write the plan concisely.

One more thing to verify: the `widget_child_count` for ZStack. `layoutOf(item)` iterates childItems looking for `isLayout`. For a plain Item, children are the two TEXT items (QQuickText), neither is a layout, so layoutOf returns null → returns item->childItems().size() = 2. Good.

Also, will render_once place children at (0,0)? A plain Item's children with no anchors: x=0,y=0 default. render_once forces layout pass. They remain 0,0. Good.

Let me also verify there's no implicit anchoring of ZStack children to fill in insertChild: the `parentId == 0` check anchors the CHILD (ZStack) to root, not the ZStack's children. For children of ZStack (parentId=1), no anchoring. Good.

Now, do I need to add any new test hook? No — position and size and child_count hooks already exist from the previous work. Great, so this test needs NO C++/header changes, just a Rust test in ffi.rs.

Wait — I should double check the position hook returns `item->x()` which for a child of a plain Item is 0. Yes.

So the plan is purely additive: one test function in ffi.rs `mod tests`, plus update status.md "Verified by".

Let me confirm the test name style and where to insert. I'll add it right after `hstack_lays_out_children_horizontally` and before `new_components_and_media_binding`.

Let me write the plan. I don't think I need to ask clarifying questions — the approach is clear and mirrors the prior two tests. But I might mention the option to also verify draw order via a new hook, and ask if they want that. Given plan mode encourages asking when weighing tradeoffs, I'll briefly note it but recommend the minimal overlap test.

Actually, let me reconsider: is overlap at (0,0) really "laid out correctly" given the spec says ZStack default alignment is top-leading (0/absent) and children keep own size? Yes: default alignment 0 = top-leading, so children position at top-leading (0,0) within the ZStack box. Children with fixed size keep that size. So (0,0) + own size is exactly the spec's default behavior. 

So the test is faithful to both the spec default and the current implementation.

Let me write the plan now. Keep concise.

I'll present:
- Where: ffi.rs mod tests (add one #[test]), status.md.

   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
 - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative qtmultimedia`).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
   `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
   core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.

   `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
   set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
   `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
 - **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
   emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
   commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
   preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
   renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
   clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
   are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
   `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.

   native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
   (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
   FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
   `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family via the `font` `QFont`
   property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible, z,
   value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
   `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
   prompt/label→placeholder, image source. **Stack alignment**: a stack's
   `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
   (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).
   **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
   `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
   slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
 - **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
   *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
   attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
   the create-time contentItem placeholder.
 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
   (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
   `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
   ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
   `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
 - **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
   is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
   its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
   Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
   spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
   `DELETE`.
 - **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
   `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
   renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
 - **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
   fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
   shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
   concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
   init.
 - **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
   `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
   C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
 - **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
   an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
   idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
 - **Asset root** (`pathland_qt_set_asset_root` /
   `pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root`): web-style `/_pathland/...` image/media
   sources resolve against a host-extracted local directory (the Qt analogue of
   `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); the Java Qt host extracts `DemoAssets` and
   sets it before `runRing`.
 - **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
   on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
   `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
   `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
   a bare program name to Qt.
 - **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
   shared ring).
 
 - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
   **Page sizing:** each page wrapper is anchored to fill the nav container
   (`placeDestination`), so the header/content/destination chain is sized and the
   destination subtree fills the content area (previously the page wrapper was
   attached unsized, collapsing the content to 0×0 and showing only an
   overflowing title).
 
 - **Post-merge protocol parity (October 2026)**: the crate was merged onto the
   shared `PARAMETER` rename and now maps the protocol surface added on `main`:
   - `ICON` (0x0B) → a `Text` item whose glyph is resolved from `ICON_NAME` by a
     renderer-owned canonical-name map (unknown names fall back to a dot), with
     `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE` reuse (spec/ICONS.md).
   - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) → **non-visual** (layout-transparent: created but
     never attached) hosting a QML `MediaPlayer` + `AudioOutput`
     (spec/MEDIA.md).
   - `VIDEO` (0x0A) → a `VideoOutput` surface; `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` binds its
     `source` to the referenced controller's `MediaPlayer` (a reference, not a
     parent/child edge).
   - `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) → a transparent vertical container.
   - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` (0x17) → a greedy two-axis slot; its one selected child
     fills it.
   - `GRID_ROW` (0x1D) → a row-grouping container whose cells flatten into
     the parent Grid.
 - **Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core`): `LIST`-typed properties
   (`FIT_QUERY`) decode into `HostNode::lists`, and `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` into
   `HostNode::date` — so the Qt layer can measure fit slots and format dates.
 - **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit measurement**: the slot's `FIT_QUERY` thresholds reach
   the C++ layer as CSV; a width change derives the fit index (largest
   `minWidth` ≤ allocated width) and reports `FIT_CHANGED` (only when it
   changes).
 - **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: a row's cells attach directly to the parent Grid
   (row-major), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.
 - **`DATE_PICKER`**: `SET_DATE` (days since epoch + millis of day) renders as an
   ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field — a QML approximation
   (Qt Quick has no native date picker).
 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md): pointer `hover`/`leave` (`POINTER_MOVE`
   hovering/leaving) from the listener `MouseArea`; `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the
   focused text input (component-type/key-listener gated); `FOCUS_CHANGED` /
   `EDITING_CHANGED` / `SUBMIT` for text inputs (gated by the matching
   `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits); BackSpace is native back unless a text input is
   focused (focus-aware, no longer deferred).
 - **Visual styling layer** (parity with the web/GTK demos):
   - `BACKGROUND_COLOR` / `BORDER_*` / `BORDER_RADIUS` render on a background
     `Rectangle` behind a container's content (stacks reuse an injected
     `pl<id>bg`; plain containers create one lazily); `Rectangle`-backed nodes
     set them directly. `RESET_NODE` clears them.
   - **Composite control mode** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §2): a `Button` that gains
     children is promoted from the native widget to a bare `Item`+`ColumnLayout`
     shell that renders the app's `ButtonStyle` body, so `PlainButtonStyle` /
     `BorderedButtonStyle` buttons look like the web/GTK ones. Leaf buttons stay
     native.
   - **Foreground inheritance** (CSS `color`): a container's `COLOR` is inherited
     by descendant `Text`/`Icon` that don't set their own.
   - **Layout defaults**: cross-axis stretch (`align-items:stretch`) when no
     `ALIGNMENT` is set; `Spacer` expands on the main axis; `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
   - **`TEXT_STYLE`** applies a base typography (size + weight) that raw
     `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT` override; **`SHADOW_*`** draws a best-effort
     offset shadow layer.
 - **Media transport** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`
   (play/pause), `MEDIA_POSITION` (seek, seconds→ms), `MEDIA_VOLUME` /
   `MEDIA_MUTED` (via `AudioOutput`), `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
   `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
   `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` reports (reported by the
   controller's component type, not gated by `BINDING_ID`; programmatic sets are
   echo-suppressed). A play/pause declared before the source is re-applied when
   the source lands.
 - **Layout/property parity**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_*`,
   `CONTENT_MODE` (image fit/fill), `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_COLOR` /
   `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_RADIUS`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`,
   `TRUNCATION_MODE`, and `GRID_COLUMNS` (via the `Layout` attached properties
   where applicable).

   implicit import path; a `cargo test` binary lives in a huge `target/debug/deps`
   and plugin resolution scanned it for minutes. The shell now drops the
   application directory from the engine's import path at init, so
   `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` completes in ~2s (no copy-to-temp workaround).
